1.1: And the Lord spake with Mosheh in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tabernacle of ordinance, on the first of the second month, in the second year of their coming out from the land of Mizraim, saying:
1.2: Take the sum of all the congregation of the children of Israel after their kindreds, and after the house of their fathers, with the number of their names, every male by their capitations:
1.3: From a son of twenty years and upwards, everyone who can go forth to war in Israel, thou and Aharon number them by their hosts.
1.4: And with you let there be a man of each tribe, a man who is chief of the house of his fathers.
1.5: And these are the names of the men who shall stand with you. Of Reuben, Elizur bar Shedeur;
1.10: Of the Beni-Joseph, of Ephraim, Elishama bar Amihud; of Menasheh, Gamliel bar Pheda-Zur;
1.16: These were the called ones of the congregation, princes of the tribes of their fathers, chiefs of the thousands of Israel were they.
1.17: And Mosheh and Aharon took these men who were expressed by their names;
1.18: And they assembled all the congregation on the first of the second month, and they declared their pedigrees according to the house of their fathers, with the number of their names from twenty years old and upwards, by their polling.
1.19: As the Lord commanded Mosheh, he numbered them in the wilderness of Sinai.
1.20: And the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel, by their generations and their families, according to the house of their fathers, with the number of their names, by their polls; every male from twenty years old and upward, all going forth in the host:
1.21: Of the tribe of Reuben were numbered forty and six thousand and five hundred.
1.22: Of the sons of Shemeon, by their generations and their families and the house of their fathers, were numbered, by the number of their names, according to their polls, every male from twenty years old and upwards, everyone going forth in the host;
1.23: Of the tribe of Shemeon, were numbered fifty and nine thousand and three hundred.
1.24: Of the sons of Gad, the generations of the families of the house of their fathers, according to the number of their names from twenty years old and upwards, everyone going forth in the host;
1.25: Of the tribe of Gad, were numbered forty and five thousand and six hundred and fifty.
1.26: Of the sons of Jehudah, the generations of the families of the house of their fathers, by the number of their names, from twenty years old and upwards, everyone going forth in the host;
1.27: Of the tribe of Jehudah, were numbered seventy and four thousand and six hundred.
1.28: Of the sons of Issakar, the generations of the families of the house of their fathers, by the number of their names, from twenty years old and upwards, everyone going forth in the host;
1.29: Of the tribe of Issakar, were numbered fifty and four thousand and four hundred.
1.30: Of the tribe of Zebulon, the generations of the families of the house of their fathers, by the number of their names, from a son of twenty years and upward, everyone going forth in the host;
1.31: Of the tribe of Zebulon, were numbered fifty and seven thousand and four hundred.
1.32: Of the sons of Joseph, the generations of the Beni-Ephraim by the kindreds of the house of their fathers, in the number of their names, from a son of twenty years and upwards, everyone going forth in the host;
1.33: Of the tribe of Ephraim, forty thousand and five hundred.
1.34: The generations of the Beni Menasheh by the kindreds of the house of their fathers, in the number of their names, from a son of twenty years and upwards, everyone going forth in the host;
1.35: Of the tribe of Menasheh, were numbered thirty and two thousand and two hundred.
1.36: The generations of the sons of Benyamin, by the kindreds of the house of their fathers, in the number of their names, from a son of twenty years and upward, everyone going forth in the host;
1.37: Of the tribe of Benyamin, were numbered thirty and five thousand and four hundred.
1.38: The generations of the Beni Dan, by the kindreds of the house of their fathers, in the number of their names, from a son of twenty years and upward, everyone going forth in the host;
1.39: Of the tribe of Dan, were numbered sixty and two thousand and seven hundred.
1.40: Of the generations or the Beni Asher, by the kindreds of the house of their fathers, in the number of their names, from a son of twenty years and upward, everyone going forth in the host;
1.41: Of the tribe of Asher, were numbered forty and one thousand and five hundred.
1.42: The generations of the sons of Naphtali, by the kindreds of the house of their fathers, in the number of their names, from a son of twenty years and upwards, everyone going forth in the host;
1.43: Of the tribe Naphtali, were numbered fifty and three thousand and four hundred.
1.44: These were the numbered ones whom Mosheh and Aharon, and the twelve men, the princes of Israel, did number, severally, according to the house of their fathers.
1.45: And all those who were numbered of the Beni Israel according to the house of their fathers, from a son of twenty years and upward, everyone going forth in the host of Israel;
1.46: All the numbered ones were six hundred and three thousand and five hundred and fifty.
1.47: But the Levites, by the tribe of their fathers, were not numbered among them.
1.48: And the Lord had spoken with Mosheh, saying:
1.49: Only the tribe of Levi thou shalt not number, nor take the account of them among the sons of Israel.
1.50: But thou shalt appoint the Levites over the tabernacle of the testimony, and over all its vessels, and over all that belongeth to it: and they shall carry the tabernacle and all its vessels, and serve it; and they shall encamp round about the tabernacle.
1.51: And when the tabernacle is to go forward, the Levites shall take it apart; and when the tabernacle is to be stationary, the Levites shall set it up; but the stranger who cometh nigh shall be put to death.
1.52: And the sons of Israel shall encamp every man upon his own dwelling-place, and every man by his standard, according to their hosts.
1.53: But the Levites shall dwell round about the tabernacle of the testimony, that there may not be wrath upon the congregation of the sons of Israel; and the Levites shall watch the watching of the tabernacle of testimony.
1.54: And the sons of Israel did according to all that the Lord commanded Mosheh, so did they.

2.1: And the Lord spake with Mosheh and with Aharon, saying:
2.2: Every man (shall encamp) by his standard, by the ensign of the house of their fathers shall the sons of Israel encamp.
2.3: Over against the tabernacle of ordinance shall they encamp round about. The standard of the camp of Jehudah shall they pitch, according to their hosts, eastward toward the sunrise: and the chief of the sons of Jehudah is Nachshon bar Aminadab.
2.4: And his host, and the number of them, seventy and four thousand and six hundred.
2.5: And they who pitch next by him shall be the tribe of Issakar; and the chief of the sons of Issakar, Nethanel bar Zuar;
2.6: And his host, and the numbered of it, fifty and four thousand and four hundred.
2.7: The tribe of Zebulon, and the chief of the sons of Zebulon, Eliab bar Chelon.
2.8: And his host, and the numbered of them, fifty and seven thousand and four hundred.
2.9: All that were numbered of the camp of Jehudah, a hundred and eighty and six thousand and four hundred, by their hosts: they shall go forward in front.
2.10: The standard of the camp of Reuben (shall be) to the south, by their hosts: and the chief of the Beni Reuben, Elizur bar Shedeur.
2.11: And his host, and the numbered of it, forty and six thousand and five hundred.
2.12: And they who pitch by him shall be the tribe of Shemeon; and the chief of the Beni Shemeon, Shelumiel bar Zuri-Shaddai;
2.13: And his host, and the numbered of them, fifty and nine thousand and three hundred.
2.14: And the tribe of Gad, and the chief of the Beni Gad, Eljasaph bar Rehuel;
2.15: And his host, and the numbered of them, forty and five thousand six hundred and fifty.
2.16: All who were numbered of the camp of Reuben, a hundred and fifty and one thousand four hundred and fifty, by their hosts: they shall go forward secondly.
2.17: But the tabernacle of ordinance shall be taken forward with the camp of the Levites, in the midst of the camp: as they encamp, so shall they go onward, every man in his place, by their standard.
2.18: The standard of the camp of Ephraim, by their hosts, shall be to the west: and the chief of the Beni-Ephraim, Elishama bar Ammihud.
2.19: And his host and their numbered ones, forty thousand and five hundred.
2.20: And they who shall be next by him shall be the tribe of Menasheh: and the chief of the Beni Menasheh, Gamliel bar Phedazur.
2.21: And his host, and the numbered thereof, thirty and two thousand and two hundred.
2.22: And the tribe of Benyamin, and the chieftain of the sons of Benyamin, Abidan bar Gideoni:
2.23: And his host, and the numbered thereof, thirty and five thousand and four hundred.
2.24: All the numbered of the camp of Ephraim were a hundred and eight thousand and one hundred, by their hosts: and they went forward thirdly.
2.25: The standard of the camp of Dan (shall be) to the north, by their hosts; and the chieftain of the Beni Dan, Achiezer bar Ammi-Shaddai.
2.26: And his host, and the numbered thereof, sixty and two thousand and seven hundred.
2.27: And those who encamp by him shall be the tribe of Asher; and the chieftain of the Beni Asher, Phagiel bar Akran.
2.28: And his host, and the numbered of it, forty and one thousand and five hundred.
2.29: And the tribe of Naphtali, and the chief of the Beni Naphtali, Achira bar Enan:
2.30: And his host, and the numbered thereof, fifty and three thousand and four hundred.
2.31: All who were numbered of the camp of Dan, a hundred and fifty and seven thousand and six hundred: they shall go hindmost by their standards.
2.32: These are they who were numbered of the sons of Israel, by the house of their fathers; all who were numbered in the camps by their hosts, six hundred and three thousand five hundred and fifty.
2.33: But the Levites were not numbered among the sons of Israel, as the Lord commanded Mosheh.
2.34: And the sons of Israel did according to all which the Lord commanded Mosheh: so did they encamp by their standards, and so went they forward every man by his family, and by the house of his fathers.

3.1: And these are the generations of Aharon and Mosheh in the day that the Lord spake with Mosheh in the mountain of Sinai.
3.2: And these; are the names of the sons of Aharon. His firstborn, Nadab; and Abihu, Elazar, and Ithamar.
3.3: These are the names of the sons of Aharon, the priests, who were consecrated that their oblations might be offered, (and that they might) minister.
3.4: But Nadab and Abihu died before the Lord; in their offering the strange fire before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai: and they had no children. And Elazar and Ithamar ministered before Aharon their father.
3.5: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
3.6: Bring the tribe of Levi near, and appoint them before Aharon the priest, that they may minister with him.
3.7: And they shall keep the watch and the charge of all the congregation by the tabernacle of ordinance to perform the service of the tabernacle.
3.8: And they shall keep all the vessels of the tabernacle of ordinance, and the charge of the sons of Israel to perform the service of the tabernacle.
3.9: And thou shalt give the Levites unto Aharon, and to his sons; they are delivered and given to him from the sons of Israel.
3.10: And thou shalt appoint Aharon and his sons, that they may keep their priesthood; but the stranger who cometh near shall be put to death.
3.11: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
3.12: And I, behold, I have brought near the Levites from among the sons of Israel instead of every firstborn that openeth the womb of the sons of Israel; and the Levites shall minister before Me.
3.13: For every firstborn is Mine; on the day that I slew every firstborn in the land of Mizraim, I sanctified before Me every firstborn in Israel from man to animal; they are Mine: I am the Lord.
3.14: And the Lord spake with Mosheh in the wilderness of Sinai, saying:
3.15: Number the sons of Levi, after the house of their fathers, by their families; every male from a month old and upward shalt thou number them.
3.16: And Mosheh numbered them according to the word of the Lord, as he had been commanded.
3.17: And these were the sons of Levi by their names: Gershon and Kehath and Merari.
3.18: And these are the names of the Beni-Gershon after their families: Lebni and Shemei.
3.19: And the Beni Kehath after their families: Amram and Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel.
3.20: And the Beni-Merari by their families, Mahali and Mushi; these are the families of the Levites after the house of their fathers.
3.21: Of Gershon were the family of Libni and the family of Shemei; these are the families of Gershon.
3.22: Those that were numbered of them, every male from the son of a month and upward, the number of them was seven thousand and five hundred.
3.23: The families of Gershon shall encamp behind the tabernacle, westward:
3.24: And the Rab of the house of the fathers of Gershon, Eljasaph bar Lael.
3.25: And the charge of the Beni-Gershon in the tabernacle of ordinance (shall be) the tent and its covering, and the hanging of the door of the tabernacle of ordinance;
3.26: And the curtains of the court, and the hanging of the gate of the court which is by the tabernacle, and by the altar round about, and the cords of it, for all its service.
3.27: And of Kehath was the family of Amram, and the family of Izhar, and the family or Hebron, and the family of Uzziel: these are the families of Kehath.
3.28: According to the number of all the males, from the son of a month and upward, eight thousand and six hundred, keeping the charge of the sanctuary.
3.29: The families of the Beni Kehath shall encamp by the side of the tabernacle, southward.
3.30: And the Rab of the house of the fathers of the Kehath families (shall be) Elizaphan bar Uzziel.
3.31: And their charge shall be the ark, and the table, and the candelabrum, and the altar, and the vessels of the sanctuary with which they minister, and the tent, (or hanging, Sam. Vers., “covering,”) and all (that pertaineth to) the service thereof.
3.32: And the chief (armarkella) who is appointed over the chiefs (rabbins) of the Levites is Elazar bar Aharon the priest: under his hand shall they be appointed who have the charge of the keeping of the sanctuary.
3.33: Of Merari, the families of Mahli and the families of Mushi.
3.34: And the numbers of them, according to the numbers of all the males, from the son of a month and upwards, six thousand and two hundred.
3.35: And the Rab of the house of the fathers of the Merari families, Zuriel bar Abichael; and they shall encamp on the side of the tabernacle northward.
3.36: And the charge for the custody of the sons of Merari shall be the boards of the tabernacle, and its bars, and its pillars, and its sockets, and all its vessels, and whatever (pertaineth) to its service;
3.37: And the pillars of the court round about, and their sockets, their pins, and their cords.
3.38: But they who encamp before the tabernacle eastward, even before the tabernacle of ordinance toward the sunrise, shall be Mosheh, and Aharon and his sons, keeping charge of the sanctuary, to watch over the children of Israel; and the stranger who cometh near shall be put to death.
3.39: All who were numbered of the Levites whom Mosheh and Aharon numbered by the word of the Lord, by their families, every male, from the son of a month and upward, twenty and two thousand.
3.40: And the Lord spake unto Mosheh, Number all the firstborn males of the children of Israel, from the son of a month upward, and the number of their names.
3.41: And thou shalt take the Levites before me, I am the Lord, instead of all the firstborn of the sons of Israel; and the cattle of the Levites instead of all the firstlings of the cattle of the Beni Israel.
3.42: And Mosheh numbered, as the Lord commanded him, all the firstborn of the sons of Israel.
3.43: And all the firstborn males, by the number of their names, from the son of a month and upward by their numbers, were twenty and two thousand two hundred and seventy and three.
3.44: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
3.45: Take the Levites instead of all the firstborn of the Beni Israel, and the cattle of the Levites instead of their cattle; and the Levites shall minister before Me: I am the Lord.
3.46: And of the redeemed ones of the two hundred and seventy and three of the sons of Israel who are more than the Levites,
3.47: Thou shalt take of each five shekels, by poll, in the shekel of the sanctuary shalt thou take; twenty mahin are a shekel.
3.48: And thou shalt give the silver of the redeemed who exceed them to Aharon and his sons.
3.49: And Mosheh took the silver of the redeemed who were more than the redeemed by the Levites.
3.50: Of the firstborn of the Beni Israel he took the silver, a thousand and three hundred and sixty-five shekels, in the shekel of the sanctuary.
3.51: And Mosheh gave the silver of the redeemed ones to Aharon and to his sons, by the Word of the Lord, as the Lord had commanded Mosheh.

4.1: And the Lord spake with Mosheh and with Aharon, saying:
4.2: Take the reckoning of the Beni Kehath from among the sons of Levi by the house of their fathers,
4.3: From thirty years and upward, unto fifty years; all that come to the host, to do the work of the tabernacle of ordinance.
4.4: And this (shall be) the service of the Beni Kehath in the tabernacle of ordinance, the Holy of Holies.
4.5: And Aharon and his sons shall enter in, what time the camp is to proceed; and they shall unloose the veil that is hung, and cover therewith the ark of the testimony,
4.6: And put over it a covering of hyacinthine skins, and overspread it with a wrapper, wholly purple, having inset its staves.
4.7: And upon the table of the presence bread they shall spread a wrapper of purple, and on it put the bowls and mortars, and the measures and cups for libations, and the bread that is ever on it;
4.8: And overspread it with a wrapper of scarlet, and cover it with a covering of hyacinth skins, having inset its staves.
4.9: And they shall take a purple wrapper, and cover the candelabrum of the light, and its lamps, and its tongs, and its snuff dishes, and all the vessels of the service by which they serve it;
4.10: And put it and all its vessels into a covering of hyacinthine skins, and set it upon a bar.
4.11: And upon the golden altar they shall spread a purple wrapper, and cover it with a covering of hyacinth skins, and fix its staves.
4.12: And they shall take all the vessels of the ministry with which they minister in the sanctuary, and put them in a cloth of purple, and cover them with a covering of hyacinth skins, and set them upon bars.
4.13: And they shall collect the cinders from the altar, and spread upon it a wrapper of crimson,
4.14: And put thereon all its vessels by which they minister upon it; censers, fleshhooks, shovels, and basins; all the vessels of the altar; and spread over it a covering of hyacinthine skins, and inset its staves.
4.15: And when Aharon and his sons have completed to cover up the sanctuary, and all the vessels of the sanctuary in the moving of the camp, the sons of Kehath shall go in to carry (them), but they shall not touch the holy things (themselves), lest they die; but these are the burden of the sons of Kehath in the tabernacle of ordinance.
4.16: And that delivered unto Elazar bar Aharon the priest (shall be) the oil for the light, and the aromatic incense, and the continual mincha, and the anointing oil, (with) the charge of all the tabernacle, and whatever belongeth to the sanctuary and its vessels.
4.17: And the Lord spake with Mosheh and with Aharon, saying:
4.18: Cut not off the tribe of the family of Kehath from among the Levites;
4.19: But do this to them, that they may live and not die, in their approach to the Holy of Holies: Let Aharon and his sons go in, and appoint each man his service and his burden.
4.20: But they shall not go in to see, when the vessels of the sanctuary are covered, lest they die.
4.21: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
4.22: Take the account of the sons of Gershon also, after the house of their fathers, by their families;
4.23: From thirty years and upwards to fifty years shalt thou number them, of all who come by companies to perform service in the tabernacle of ordinance.
4.24: This is the service or the family of Gershon, to serve and to carry.
4.25: And they shall carry the curtains of the tabernacle, and the tent of the tabernacle of ordinance, its covering, and the covering of hyacinth which is over it above, and the hanging for the door of the tabernacle of ordinance;
4.26: And the curtains of the court, and the hanging that is at the entrance of the court, which is by the tabernacle and by the altar round about, and their cords, and all the instruments of their service; and with all that is delivered to them they shall perform their service.
4.27: By the word of Aharon and his sons shall be all the service of the Beni-Gershon, with all their burdens, and all their employment; and you shall appoint them in charge with all their burdens.
4.28: This is the service of the family of the Beni-Gershon in the tabernacle of ordinance, and their charge shall be under the hand of Ithamar bar Aharon the priest.
4.29: The sons of Merari number thou after the families of their father’s house;
4.30: From a son of thirty years and upward unto fifty years, shalt thou number them, of all who come by companies to perform the service of the tabernacle of ordinance.
4.31: And this is the charge of their burthen of all the service in the tabernacle of ordinance; the boards of the tabernacle, and its bars, and its pillars, and their bases;
4.32: And the columns of the court round about, their bases, pins, and cords of all the instruments of all their service; and by their names you shall number the instruments of the charge of their burthen.
4.33: This is the ministry of the family of the Beni-Merari, after all their service in the tabernacle of ordinance under the hand of Ithamar bar Aharon the priest.
4.34: And Mosheh and Aharon and the chiefs of the congregation numbered the sons of Kehath, by their families, and by the house of their fathers;
4.35: From a son of thirty years and upward to fifty years; everyone who came with the band to the service in the tabernacle of ordinance.
4.36: And they who were numbered of them by their families, were two thousand seven hundred and fifty.
4.37: These are the numbered of the family of Kehath, everyone serving in the tabernacle of ordinance, whom Mosheh and Aharon numbered upon the Word of the Lord, by the hand of Mosheh.
4.38: And the numbered of the sons of Gershon after the families of their father’s house,
4.39: from thirty years and upwards to fifty years, everyone who cometh with the band to the service of the tabernacle of ordinance,
4.40: even those who were numbered of them by their families of their father’s house, were two thousand six hundred and thirty.
4.41: These are the numbered of the Beni-Gershon, everyone who did service in the tabernacle of ordinance, whom Mosheh and Aharon numbered by the mouth of the Word of the Lord.
4.42: And the numbered of the Beni-Merari, by the families of their father’s house,
4.43: from thirty years and upward to fifty years, all who come by bands to serve in the tabernacle of ordinance,
4.44: even they who were numbered by their families, were three thousand and two hundred.
4.45: These are they who were numbered in the families of the Beni-Merari, whom Mosheh and Aharon numbered by the mouth of the Word of the Lord, by the hand of Mosheh.
4.46: All the numbered ones of the Levites whom Mosheh and Aharon and the chiefs of Israel numbered, by their families, and by the house of their fathers,
4.47: From thirty years and upward to fifty years, all who came to minister the ministry of the service, and the work of carrying in the tabernacle of ordinance,
4.48: even the numbered of them were eight thousand five hundred and eighty.
4.49: Upon the Word of the Lord they were numbered by the hand of Mosheh; every man according to his service and his burthen they were numbered, as the Lord commanded Mosheh.

5.1: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
5.2: Command the sons of Israel to send away from the camp everyone who is leprous, and everyone who hath an issue, and everyone who is defiled with the pollution of the life of man:
5.3: From male to female you, shall send them away, that they defile not their camps; for My Shekinah dwelleth among you.
5.4: And the sons of Israel did so; as the Lord spake with Mosheh, so did the sons of Israel.
5.5: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
5.6: When a man or a woman hath committed any of the sins of mankind to prevaricate prevarication before the Lord, and that man hath become guilty;
5.7: They shall make confession of the sin which they have committed, and restore the principal of (the property of) the trespass, and add a fifth part thereto, and give to him against whom the sin was committed;
5.8: But if the man (hath deceased, or) hath no kinsman unto whom the trespass should be returned, let the trespass be restored before the Lord unto the priest, besides the ram of atonement which shall be offered to atone for him.
5.9: And all separated things of all the consecrations of the sons of Israel which are offered by the priest are his.
5.10: And the consecrated tenths of every man shall be his, and whatsoever a man giveth unto the priest shall be his.
5.11: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
5.12: Speak with the sons of Israel, and say to them: If a man’s wife go astray and prevaricate against him prevarication,
5.13: And a man lie with her, and it be hidden from her husband’s eyes, and she be contaminated, and there be no witness against her, and she be not convicted (or apprehended);
5.14: But the spirit of jealousy come upon him, and he be jealous of his wife that she hath been defiled; or the spirit of jealousy come upon him, and he become jealous of his wife, though she be not defiled;
5.15: Then shall the man bring his wife to the priest, and bring her offering for her, a tenth part of three seins of barley flour; he shall pour no oil thereon, nor put frankincense upon it, because it is a mincha of jealousy, a mincha of remembrance, bringing sins to remembrance.
5.16: And the priest shall bring her near, and make her stand before the Lord.
5.17: And the priest shall take water from the laver in an earthen vessel. And the priest shall take from the dust which is on the floor of the tabernacle, and put it into the water.
5.18: And the priest shall make the woman stand before the Lord, and shall uncover the woman’s head, and put the mincha of remembrance, the mincha of jealousy, upon her hands; and in the priest’s hand shall be the bitter waters of cursing.
5.19: And the priest shall adjure her, and say to the woman: If no man hath lain with thee, and if thou bast not gone astray to uncleanness (with another) instead of thy husband, be thou unhurt (zakaah, innocent, clean) from these bitter waters of cursing.
5.20: But if thou hast gone astray (to another) instead of thy husband, and art defiled; and another man hath lain with thee, besides thy husband,
5.21: the priest shall adjure the woman by the oath of the curse; and the priest shall say to the woman: The Lord set thee for a curse and an execration in the midst of thy people, by the Lord making thy thigh to be corrupt, and thy bowels to swell.
5.22: And these waters of cursing shall enter thy inside, to make thy bowels to swell, and thy thigh to become corrupt. And the woman shall say, Amen, Amen!
5.23: And the priest shall write these maledictions upon a book, and shall wash them out with the bitter waters.
5.24: And he shall make the woman to drink the bitter waters of cursing; and the waters of the curse shall enter into her unto bitterness.
5.25: And the priest shall take from the woman’s hand the mincha of jealousy; and wave the mincha before the Lord, and offer it upon the altar.
5.26: And the priest shall take with a full hand from the mincha the memorial of it, and burn it upon the altar; and afterward the woman shall drink the water.
5.27: And when he hath made her drink the water, it shall be that if she hath been defiled and hath wrought perverseness with her husband, the waters of the execration will enter into her with bitterness, and her bowels will swell, and her thigh become corrupt: and the woman shall be for an execration among her people.
5.28: But if the woman hath not been defiled, but is innocent, they shall enter harmlessly, and she shall conceive with conception.
5.29: This is the law of jealousy, when a woman hath gone astray from her husband,
5.30: or when the spirit of jealousy passeth upon a man, and he become jealous of his wife. He shall make the wife stand before the Lord; and the priest shall do for him (according to) all this law.
5.31: And the man shall be innocent from guilt, but the woman shall bear her sin.

6.1: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
6.2: Speak with the children of Israel, and say to them: When a man or a woman would be separated by a vow of the Nazira, to be devoted before the Lord;
6.3: He shall abstain from wine, (whether) new or old; vinegar of new wine or vinegar of old wine he may not drink; neither of anything expressed from grapes may he drink; nor of grapes, either fresh or dried, may he eat.
6.4: All the days of his nazirate he may not eat of aught that is produced by the vine (wine tree), from its kernels to its expressed juice.
6.5: All the days of his nazir vow a razor shall not pass upon his head; until the days be fulfilled which he should devote before the Lord, he shall be consecrate; he shall let the hair of his head grow.
6.6: All the days of his vow before the Lord; he shall come near no dead person:
6.7: For his father or his mother, for his brother or his sister, should they die, he shall not make himself unclean; because the consecration of Eloha is upon his head:
6.8: All the days of his nazirhood shall he be consecrate before the Lord.
6.9: And if anyone with him die suddenly (to him) unawares, and he defile the head of his vow, let him shave his head on the day of his purification, on the seventh day let him shave it:
6.10: And on the eighth day let him bring two turtle doves or two young pigeons unto the priest, to the door of the tabernacle of ordinance.
6.11: And let the priest make one a sin offering, and one a burnt offering, to atone for him; for that he had sinned by the dead; and let him consecrate his head (anew) on that day.
6.12: And he shall devote before the Lord the days of his nazirhood, and bring a lamb of the year for a trespass offering: but the former days have been in vain, because he hath defiled his vow.
6.13: And this is the law of the Nazirite on the day that the days of his vow are fulfilled. He shall be brought to the door of the tabernacle of ordinance;
6.14: And shall present his oblation before the Lord, a lamb of the year, one unblemished, for a burnt offering, and one ewe lamb of the year, unblemished, for a sin offering; and one ram unblemished for a consecrated oblation;
6.15: and a basket of unleavened bread, cakes of flour mingled with oil, and unleavened wafers anointed with oil, their minchas and their libations.
6.16: And the priest shall present them before the Lord; and make the sin offering and the burnt offering,
6.17: And the ram he shall make a consecrated oblation before the Lord with the basket of unleavened cakes; and the priest shall make the mincha, and the libation therewith.
6.18: And let the Nazirite, at the door of the tabernacle of ordinance, shave his consecrated head; and take the hair of his consecrated head and lay it upon the fire which is under the cauldron, for the peace offerings.
6.19: And the priest shall take the boiled shoulder of the ram, and one of the unleavened cakes from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and put (them) upon the hands of the Nazirite after the shaving of his consecration.
6.20: And the priest shall uplift them, an elevation before the Lord. It shall be dedicated to the priest, with the breast of the elevation, and the shoulder of the separation; and after that the Nazirite may drink wine.
6.21: This is the law of the Nazirite, who hath vowed his oblation before the Lord, for his consecration, besides those which may come to his hand; according to the vow which he hath vowed, so shall he do according to the law of his consecration.
6.22: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
6.23: Speak with Aharon and with his sons, saying: Thus shall you bless the children of Israel, and shall say unto them:
6.24: The Lord bless thee and keep thee.
6.25: The Lord make His Shekinah to shine upon thee, and be merciful to thee.
6.26: The Lord turn away His displeasure from thee, and bestow upon thee peace.
6.27: And they shall bestow the benediction of My Name upon the sons of Israel, and I will bless them.

7.1: And it was on the day when Mosheh had completed to set up the tabernacle, and to anoint it, and to consecrate it, and all its vessels, and had anointed and sanctified them,
7.2: That the princes of Israel, heads of the house of their fathers, the chiefs of the tribes, who had been appointed over them who were numbered,
7.3: came near, and brought their oblations before the Lord. Six covered wagons and twelve oxen; a wagon for two of the princes, and an ox for each one: and they brought them before the tabernacle.
7.4: And the Lord spake to Mosheh, saying:
7.5: Take (the waggons) from them, that they may be for the work of the service of the tabernacle of ordinance; and thou shalt give them to the Levites, to each man according to the need of his work.
7.6: And Mosheh took the waggons and the oxen, and gave them to the Levites.
7.7: Two waggons and four oxen gave he to the sons of Gershon, according to the need of their work;
7.8: And four waggons and eight oxen he gave to the sons of Merari, according to the need of their work, by the hand of Ithamar bar Aharon the priest.
7.9: But to the sons of Kehath he gave not, because they had the work of the sanctuary, and carried upon their shoulders.
7.10: And the princes offered at the dedication (chanucha) of the altar on the day that they anointed it, and the princes presented their oblations before the altar.
7.11: And the Lord said to Mosheh, One prince shall offer, on each day of the dedication of the altar.
7.12: And he who offered his oblation on the first day was Nachshon bar Aminadab, of the tribe of Jehudah:
7.13: And his offering was, one bowl of silver, a hundred and thirty shekels was its weight; one silver vase, seventy shekels in weight, in shekels of the sanctuary; both of them filled with flour, mingled with oil, for a mincha;
7.14: One pan (censer) weighing ten shekels; it was of gold, filled with fragrant incense;
7.15: One young bullock, one ram, one lamb of the year for a burnt offering;
7.16: One kid of the goats for a sin offering;
7.17: And for consecrated oblations, two oxen, five rams, five goats, five lambs of the year. This was the oblation of Nachshon bar Aminadab.
7.18: On the second day offered Nethanel bar Zuar, prince of the tribe of Issakar.
7.19: He offered his oblation, one silver bowl, a hundred and thirty shekels was its weight; one silver vase, its weight seventy shekels, in the shekels of the sanctuary; both of them filled with flour sprinkled with oil for a mincha;
7.20: One pan weighing ten shekels; it was of gold, full of fragrant incense;
7.21: One young bullock, one ram, one lamb of the year for a burnt offering,
7.22: One kid of the goats for a sin offering;
7.23: And for a sacrifice of consecrated things, two oxen, five rams, five goats, five lambs of the year. This was the oblation of Nethanel bar Zuar.
7.24: On the third day, the prince of the Beni Zebulon, Eliab bar Chelon.
7.25: His offering, one silver bowl, its weight one hundred and thirty shekels; one silver vase, its weight seventy shekels in the shekels of the sanctuary; both of them filled with flour mingled with oil for a mincha;
7.26: One pan weighing ten shekels; it was of gold, and filled with fragrant incense;
7.27: One young bullock, one lamb of the year for a burnt offering,
7.28: One kid of the goats for a sin offering;
7.29: And for consecrated offerings, two oxen, five rams, five goats, five lambs of the year. This was the oblation of Eliab bar Chelon.
7.30: On the fourth day the prince of the sons of Reuben, Elizur bar Shedeur.
7.31: His offering, one silver bowl, one hundred and thirty shekels its weight, one silver vase, weighing seventy shekels in the shekels of the sanctuary, both of them filled with flour sprinkled with oil for a mincha;
7.32: One pan weighing ten shekels; it was of gold, and filled with fragrant incense;
7.33: One young bullock, one ram, one lamb of the year for a burnt offering,
7.34: One kid of the goats for a sin offering;
7.35: And for the consecrated oblation, two oxen, five rams, five goats, five lambs of the year. This was the oblation of Elizur bar Shedeur.
7.36: On the fifth day the prince of the Beni Shemeon, Shelumiel bar Zurishaddai.
7.37: His offering, one silver bowl, one hundred and thirty, shekels was its weight, one silver vase, weighing seventy shekels in the shekels of the sanctuary, both of them filled with flour mingled with oil for a mincha;
7.38: One pan weighing ten shekels; it was of gold, filled with fragrant incense;
7.39: One young bullock, one ram, one lamb of the year for a burnt offering,
7.40: One kid of the goats for a sin offering;
7.41: And for consecrated oblations two oxen, five rams, five goats, five lambs of the year. This was the oblation of Shelumiel bar Zurishaddai.
7.42: On the sixth day the prince of the sons of Gad, Eljasaph bar Dehuel.
7.43: His offering, one silver bowl, its weight one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver vase, weighing seventy shekels in shekels of the sanctuary, both filled with flour sprinkled with oil for a mincha;
7.44: One pan weighing ten shekels of gold, full of fragrant incense;
7.45: One young bullock, one ram, one lamb of the year for a burnt offering,
7.46: One kid of the goats for a sin offering;
7.47: And for consecrated oblations, two oxen, five rams, five goats, five lambs of the year. This was the oblation of Eljasaph bar Dehuel.
7.48: On the seventh day the prince of the sons of Ephraim, Elishama bar Ammihud.
7.49: His offering, one silver bowl weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver vase weighing seventy shekels in shekels of the sanctuary, both of them filled with flour sprinkled with oil for a mincha;
7.50: One pan weighing ten shekels of gold, filled with fragrant incense;
7.51: One young bullock, one ram, one Iamb of the year, for a burnt offering;
7.52: One kid of the goats for a sin offering;
7.53: And for consecrated oblations, two oxen, five rams, five goats, five Iambs of the year. This was the oblation of Elishama bar Ammihud.
7.54: On the eighth day the prince of the Beni Menashe, Gamliel bar Phedazur.
7.55: His offering, one silver bowl, weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver vase, weighing seventy shekels in shekels of the sanctuary, both of them filled with flour sprinkled with oil for a mincha;
7.56: One pan weighing ten shekels of gold, filled with fragrant incense;
7.57: One young bullock, one ram, one lamb of the year, for a burnt offering;
7.58: One kid of the goats for a sin offering;
7.59: And for consecrated oblations, two oxen, five rams, five goats, five lambs of the year. This was the oblation of Gamliel bar Phedazur.
7.60: On the ninth day the prince of the sons of Benyamin, Abidan bar Gideoni.
7.61: His oblation, one silver bowl, weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver vase, weighing seventy shekels in shekels of the sanctuary, both of them filled with flour sprinkled with oil for a mincha;
7.62: One pall weighing ten shekels of gold, filled with fragrant incense;
7.63: One young bullock, one ram, one lamb of the year, for a burnt offering;
7.64: One kid of the goats for a sin offering;
7.65: And for consecrated oblations, two oxen, five rams, five goats, five lambs of the year. This was the oblation of Abidan bar Gideoni.
7.66: On the tenth day the prince of the sons of Dan, Achiezer bar Amishaddai.
7.67: His oblation, one silver bowl, weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver vase, weighing seventy shekels in shekels of the sanctuary, both of them filled with flour sprinkled with oil for a mincha;
7.68: One pan weighing ten shekels of gold, filled with fragrant incense;
7.69: One young bullock, one ram, one lamb of the year, for a burnt offering;
7.70: One kid of the goats for a sin offering;
7.71: And for consecrated oblations, two oxen, five rams, five goats, five lambs of the year. This was the oblation of Achiezer bar Amishaddai.
7.72: On the eleventh day the prince of the Beni Asher, Phagiel bar Akran.
7.73: His oblation, one silver bowl, weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver vase, weighing seventy shekels in shekels of the sanctuary, both of them filled with flour sprinkled with oil for a mincha;
7.74: one pan weighing ten shekels of gold, filled with fragrant incense;
7.75: One young bullock, one ram, one lamb of the year, for a burnt offering;
7.76: One kid of the goats for a sin offering;
7.77: And for consecrated oblations two oxen, five rams, five goats, five lambs of the year. This was the oblation of Phagiel bar Akran.
7.78: On the twelfth day, the prince of the Beni Naphtali, Achira bar Enan.
7.79: His oblation, one silver bowl, weighing one hundred and thirty shekels, one silver vase, weighing seventy shekels in shekels of the sanctuary, both of them filled with flour sprinkled with oil for a mincha;
7.80: One pan weighing ten shekels of gold, filled with fragrant incense;
7.81: One young bullock, one ram, one lamb of the year, for a burnt offering;
7.82: One kid of the goats for a sin offering;
7.83: And for consecrated oblations two oxen, five rams, five goats, five lambs of the year. This was the oblation of Achira bar Enan.
7.84: This was the dedication of the altar, on the day that they anointed it. By the princes of Israel (were offered) twelve silver bowls, twelve silver vases, twelve golden censers;
7.85: One hundred and thirty shekels was the weight of one silver bowl, and seventy that of one silver vase: all the silver vessels weighed two thousand four hundred shekels in shekels of the sanctuary.
7.86: The golden censers were twelve, full of fragrant incense, weighing each ten shekels; the weight of the censers was, in shekels of the sanctuary, all the gold of the censers one hundred and twenty (shekels).
7.87: All the bullocks for the burnt offering were twelve bullocks, rams twelve, lambs of the year twelve, and their minchas. And for the sin offering twelve kids of the goats.
7.88: And all the oxen for consecrated victims were twenty-four oxen, rams sixty, goats sixty, lambs of the year sixty. This was the Dedication of the Altar after they had anointed it.
7.89: And when Mosheh had gone into the tabernacle of ordinance to speak with Him, then heard he the Voice of Him who spake with him from above the Mercy Seat over the Ark of the Testimony, between the two Kerubaia; and He spake unto him.

8.1: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
8.2: Speak with Aharon, and say to him: When thou dost kindle the lamps upon the face of the candelabrum, the seven lamps shall be burning (together).
8.3: And Aharon did so: on the face of the candelabrum he made the lamps burn, as the Lord commanded Mosheh.
8.4: And this work of the candelabrum was of beaten gold, from its shaft to its lilies, beaten (gold) according to the pattern which the Lord had showed to Mosheh, so had he made the candelabrum.
8.5: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
8.6: Bring near the Levites from among the sons of Israel, and purify them.
8.7: And thus shalt thou do to them to purify them. Sprinkle upon them the water of purification, and make the razor to pass over all their flesh, and let them wash their vestments, and they shall be clean.
8.8: And let them take a young bullock, and his mincha of flour, sprinkled with oil; and a second bullock, a young bullock shalt thou take, for the sin offering.
8.9: And bring the Levites before the tabernacle of ordinance, and assemble all the congregation of the children of Israel.
8.10: And thou shalt bring the Levites before the Lord; and the sons of Israel shall lay their hands upon the Levites;
8.11: And Aharon shall offer the Levites as an elevation before the Lord from the sons of Israel, that they may perform the service of the Lord.
8.12: And the Levites shall lay their hands upon the head of the bullocks, and make the one for a sin offering, and the other for a burnt offering, before the Lord, to make an atonement for the Levites.
8.13: And thou shalt set the Levites before Aharon, and before his sons, and offer them up (as) an elevation before the Lord.
8.14: And thou shalt thus separate the Levites from among the sons of Israel, that the Levites may minister before Me.
8.15: And afterward shall the Levites enter, to minister (in) the tabernacle of ordinance; for thou wilt have purified them, and offered them up as an elevation.
8.16: For by a separation are they separated unto Me from among the sons of Israel, instead of every firstborn who openeth the womb of all the children of Israel have I taken them (to be) before Me.
8.17: For Mine are all the firstborn of the children of Israel, of man and of beast: in the day that I slew all the firstborn in the land of Mizraim did I sanctify them before Me.
8.18: And I have taken the Levites instead of all the firstborn of the sons of Israel.
8.19: And the Levites I have given as a gift unto Aharon and to his sons, from among the sons of Israel, to minister the service for the children of Israel in the tabernacle of ordinance, and to make atonement for the children of Israel, that death may not be among the children of Israel when the children of Israel come nigh to the sanctuary.
8.20: And Mosheh and Aharon, and all the congregation of the sons of Israel, did unto the Levites according to all that the Lord commanded Mosheh for the Levites; so did the sons of Israel to them.
8.21: And the Levites were purified, and they cleansed their raiment, and Aharon offered them (as) an elevation before the Lord; and Aharon made an atonement for them to purify them.
8.22: And afterwards the Levites went in to perform their service in the tabernacle of ordinance before Aharon and before his sons; as the Lord had commanded Mosheh concerning the Levites, so did they unto them.
8.23: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
8.24: This is (the law) of the Levites: from a son of five-and-twenty years and upward he shall come with the bands in their service (in the) tabernacle of ordinance,
8.25: and from fifty years old he shall return from the company of the ministers, and work no longer;
8.26: But minister with his brethren at the tabernacle of ordinance in keeping the custody; yet the service he shall not perform: so shalt thou do with the Levites in their charge.

9.1: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, in the wilderness of Sinai, in the second year of their going forth from the land of Mizraim, in the first month, saying:
9.2: Let the children of Israel perform the Pascha in its time.
9.3: On the fourteenth day of this month, between the suns, they shall perform it in its time according to all the rites of it, and according to all the form of it shall they do it.
9.4: And Mosheh spake with the sons of Israel to perform the Pascha.
9.5: And they performed the Pascha in Nisan, on the fourteenth day of the month, between the suns, in the wilderness of Sinai; according to all that the Lord had commanded Mosheh, so did the children of Israel.
9.6: But there were men who were unclean by defilement, (having touched) the body of a (dead) man, and they could not make the Pascha on that day; and they came before Mosheh and before Aharon that day,
9.7: And the men said to him: We are unclean, by the defilement of the life of a man, and are, therefore, restrained from offering the oblation of the Lord in its time among the sons of Israel.
9.8: And Mosheh said to them, Wait, till I shall have heard what will be commanded from before the Lord about your case.
9.9: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
9.10: Speak with the sons of Israel, saying: If any man be unclean by the defilement of the life of a man, or be in the way, afar off’ from you or from your dwellings, he shall perform the Pascha before the Lord
9.11: in the second month, on the fourteenth day, between the suns, they shall perform it; with unleavened (bread) and with bitter (herbs) shall they eat it:
9.12: They shall not leave of it till the morning, and a bone of it shall not be broken; according to all the rites of the Pascha shall they perform it.
9.13: But the man who is clean, and is not upon a journey, and forbeareth to perform the Pascha, that man shall be cut off from his people: because he hath not offered the Lord’s oblation in its time, that man shall bear his guilt.
9.14: And if a stranger sojourn with you, and will perform the Pascha before the Lord, according to the rites of the Pascha, and according to the forms thereof, so shall he do: one statute shall you have, for the stranger, and for the native of the land.
9.15: And on the day that the Tabernacle was erected the Cloud covered the Tabernacle of the Testimony; and at evening there was upon the Tabernacle as the vision of Fire, until the morning.
9.16: So was it continually; the Cloud covered it (by day), and the appearance of the Fire in the night.
9.17: And according as the Cloud was uplifted above the Tabernacle, the sons of Israel afterward went on; and at the place where the Cloud rested, there did the sons of Israel encamp.
9.18: By the Word of the Lord the sons of Israel journeyed, and by the Word of the Lord they encamped; all the days that the Cloud rested, they remained.
9.19: However long the time the Cloud was upon the Tabernacle, (however) many the days, the sons of Israel kept the watch of the Word of the Lord, and journeyed not.
9.20: And if the Cloud was over the tabernacle a number of days, according to the Word of the Lord they remained, and by the Word of the Lord they went forward.
9.21: Or if the Cloud was (over the Tabernacle only) from the evening till the morn, and the Cloud was uplifted in the morning, they went forward; whether (in the) days or nights the Cloud was uplifted, they went forward;
9.22: Whether it was two days, or a month, or a longer season, (time by time,) the Cloud was in staying upon the Tabernacle to remain thereon, the children of Israel remained, and went not forward; but at the lifting up of it they proceeded.
9.23: By the Word of the Lord they abode, and by the Word of the Lord they proceeded; they observed the watch of the Word of the Lord, upon the Word of the Lord through Mosheh.

10.1: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
10.2: Make thee two trumpets of silver, beaten shalt thou make them, and they shall be for thee to convoke the assembly, and to move forward the host.
10.3: And they shall blow with them, and bring all the congregation together unto thee, at the door of the tabernacle of ordinance.
10.4: And if they blow with but one, the chiefs, the heads of thousands of Israel, shall gather together to thee.
10.5: When you blow with a full note, (or alarm,) the host that encampeth eastward shall go forward,
10.6: and when you blow with the second alarm, the hosts that encamp southward shall go on; an alarm shall they blow for their journeys.
10.7: But when the congregation is to be gathered together, you shall blow, but not with the alarm.
10.8: And the sons of Aharon, the priests, are to blow with the trumpets; and this shall be to you a perpetual statute for your generations.
10.9: And when you enter upon the battle fight for your country, with the oppressors who oppress you, ye shall blow the alarm with the trumpets, that your remembrance may come for good before the Lord your God, (and) that you may be delivered from them who hate you.
10.10: And on the day of your rejoicing, and on your solemnities, and at the beginning of your months, ye shall blow with the trumpets over your burnt offerings, and over your consecrated victims; and they shall be for a memorial before your God: I am the Lord your God.
10.11: And it was in the second year, in the second month, on the twentieth day of the month, that the Cloud was uplifted from above the Tabernacle of the Testimony,
10.12: And the children of Israel went forward upon their journeys from the wilderness of Sinai; and the Cloud rested in the wilderness of Pharan.
10.13: And they went forward at the first by the Word of the Lord through Mosheh.
10.14: In the first place the standard of the camp of the Beni Jehudah went forward by their hosts; and over the host was Nachshon bar Aminadab.
10.15: And over the host of the tribe of the Beni Issakar, Nethanel bar Zuar.
10.16: And over the host of the tribe of the Beni Zebulun, Eliab bar Chelon.
10.17: And the tabernacle was taken down, and the sons of Gershon went forward, and the sons of Merari, carrying the tabernacle.
10.18: And the standard (or order) of the camp of Reuben went forward by their hosts, and over its host was Elizur bar Shedeur:
10.19: And over the host of the tribe of the Beni Shemeun was Shelumiel bar Zurishaddai.
10.20: And over the host of the Beni Gad was Eljasaph bar Dehuel.
10.21: And the sons of Kehath went forward, carrying the sanctuary, and (the Gershonites and sons of Merari) set up the tabernacle against they came.
10.22: And the standard of the camps of the Beni-Ephraim went forward by their hosts, and over his host was Elishama bar Amihud.
10.23: And over the host of the tribe of the Beni Menasheh was Gamliel bar Phedazur.
10.24: And over the host of the tribe of the Beni Benyamin, Abidan bar Gideoni.
10.25: And the standard of the camps of the Beni Dan went forward collecting each camp according to their hosts; and over his host was Achiezer bar Amishaddai.
10.26: And over the host of the tribe of the Beni Asher, Phagiel bar Akran;
10.27: And over the host of the tribe of the Beni Naphtali, Achira bar Enan.
10.28: These are the journeys of the sons of Israel, and according to their hosts they went forward.
10.29: And Mosheh said unto Hobab bar Reuel, the Midianite, the father-in-law of Mosheh, We are journeying to the place of which the Lord hath said, I will give it unto you: come thou with us, and we will do thee good; for the Lord hath spoken, to bring good upon Israel.
10.30: But he said to him, I will not go (with you), but to my country and to my kindred will I go.
10.31: And he said, Leave us not, I beseech thee; for thou knowest how we should encamp in the wilderness; and the great things that will be done for us thou wilt see with thine eyes.
10.32: And it shall be that if thou wilt go with us, with the good by which the Lord shall do us good, will we do good to thee.
10.33: And from the mountain on which the glory of the Lord had been revealed they went forward, journeying three days; and the ark of the Lord’s covenant went before them, three days’ journey, to provide for them a place of encampment.
10.34: And the Cloud of Glory of the Lord overspread them by day as they went forth from their encampments.
10.35: And when the ark went forward, Mosheh said: Reveal thyself, O Lord, that Thine enemies may be scattered, and Thy adversaries may flee before thee.
10.36: And when it rested, he said: Return, O Lord, and dwell in Thy glory among the multitudes of the thousands of Israel.

11.1: But the people were discontented (or, were fomenting evil) before the Lord; and it was heard before the Lord, and His anger was strongly moved, and a fire was kindled against them from before the Lord, and it consumed the outskirts of the camp.
11.2: And the people cried unto Mosheh, and Mosheh prayed before the Lord, and the fire was subdued.
11.3: And Mosheh called the name of that place Enkindlement; because the fire had been kindled against them from before the Lord.
11.4: And the mixed multitude who were among them demanded with demand; and the children of Israel also turned, and wept, and said: Who will feed us with flesh?
11.5: We remember the fish which we ate in Mizraim freely, the cucumbers and melons, the cresses and onions and garlick.
11.6: But now our soul longeth, yet there is nothing before our eyes but manna.
11.7: Now the manna was like the seed of coriander, and its appearance as the appearance of bedilcha.
11.8: And the people went about and gathered; and he who would ground it in mills, or he who would beat it in the mortar, and they dressed it in the pan, and made cakes of it, and its taste was like the taste of a confection of oil.
11.9: And when the dew came down upon the camp at night, the manna descended upon it.
11.10: And Mosheh heard the people lamenting with their families, a man at the door of his tent. And the displeasure of the Lord grew very strong, as in the eyes of Mosheh it was evil.
11.11: And Mosheh said before the Lord, Wherefore hast Thou done painfully to Thy servant, and why have I not found mercy before Thee, that Thou hast put the burden of all this people upon me?
11.12: Am I father to all this people, or are they my children, that Thou hast said to me, Carry them in thy strength, as the nurse carrieth the suckling, unto the land which Thou hast covenanted to their fathers?
11.13: Whence shall I have flesh to give to all this people? For they lament to me, saying: Give us flesh to eat.
11.14: I am not able to bear all this people alone, because it is too heavy for me.
11.15: And if Thou do thus with me, kill me, I pray, if I have found mercy before Thee, that I may not see my wretchedness.
11.16: And the Lord said to Mosheh, Gather unto Me seventy men of the elders of Israel, whom thou knowest to be elders of the people, and the overseers thereof, and bring them to the tabernacle of ordinance, and let them stand there with thee;
11.17: And I will reveal Myself, and will speak with thee there; and I will make enlargement of the Spirit that is upon thee, and put it upon them, that they may bear with thee the burden of the people, and thou mayest not sustain it by thyself alone.
11.18: And say thou to the people, Prepare yourselves for the morrow, and you shall eat flesh; for that you have lamented before the Lord, saying: Who will give us flesh, that we may eat? For it was better with us in Mizraim; and I will give you flesh, and you shall eat.
11.19: Not one day shall you eat (it), nor two days, nor five days, nor ten days, nor twenty days;
11.20: But for a month of days, until you loathe it, and it be an offence to you; because you have felt, dislike to the Word of the Lord, whose Shekinah dwelleth among you; and before whom you have wept, saying: Why came we out of Mizraim?
11.21: But Mosheh said, The people among whom I am are six hundred thousand footmen; and Thou hast said, I will give them flesh to eat for a month of days.
11.22: Shall the oxen and sheep be slaughtered for them, to satisfy them, or all the fish of the sea be gathered that they may be satisfied?
11.23: And the Lord said to Mosheh: Is the Word of the Lord restrained? Now shalt thou see whether My saying come to pass with thee or not.
11.24: And Mosheh went forth, and told the people the words of the Lord, and gathered together seventy men of the elders of the people, and set them round about the tabernacle.
11.25: And the Lord was revealed in the Cloud, and spake with him, and he made enlargement of the Spirit that was upon him, and imparted to the seventy men, the elders; and it came to pass that when the Spirit of prophecy rested upon them they prophesied, and ceased not.
11.26: But two men remained in the camp, the name of the one Eldad, and the name of the second Medad; and the Spirit of prophecy rested upon them; and, though they were in the writings, they had not come out of the camp; but they prophesied in the camp.
11.27: And a young man ran, and showed to Mosheh, and said: Eldad and Medad do prophesy in the camp.
11.28: And Jehoshua bar Nun, the minister of Mosheh from his youth, answered and said, Ribboni Mosheh, put them in bond.
11.29: But Mosheh said, Art thou jealous for my sake? I would that all the people of the Lord did prophesy, and that the Lord would confer the Spirit of prophecy upon them.
11.30: And Mosheh returned to the camp, he and the elders of Israel.
11.31: And the wind proceeded from before the Lord, and the quails flew abroad from the sea, and it bare them upon the camp as (the breadth of) a day’s journey here, and a day’s journey there, round about the camp, and as at a height of two cubits over the face of the ground.
11.32: And the people were up all that day, and all the night, and all the day after it, and collected the quails; he who collected least (gathered together) ten heaps; and they spread them abroad, round about the camp.
11.33: While yet the flesh was between their teeth, and they had not yet finished, the displeasure of the Lord was manifested strongly against the people, and the Lord inflicted death among the people with a very great mortality.
11.34: And he called the name of that place, The Graves of the Demanders; because there they buried the people who demanded.
11.35: From the Graves of the Demanders the people journeyed to Hatseroth, and they were in Hatseroth.

12.1: And Miriam and Aharon spake against Mosheh, because of the fair woman whom he had taken, because the fair woman who had been sent away he had taken.
12.2: And they said, Hath the Lord spoken only with Mosheh? Hath He not spoken with us also? And it was heard before the Lord.
12.3: (But the man Mosheh was very humble, more than all the men who were upon the face of the earth.)
12.4: And the Lord spake suddenly with Mosheh, and to Aharon and to Miriam: Come forth, you three, to the tabernacle of ordinance; and those three went forth.
12.5: And the Lord was revealed in the pillar of the Cloud, and stood at the door of the tabernacle: and He called Aharon and Miriam, and they two came forth.
12.6: And He said, Hear now My words. If there be prophets with you, I the Lord will reveal Myself (to them) in visions, in dreams will I speak with them.
12.7: But not so (with) My servant Mosheh; over all My house faithful is he.
12.8: Speaker with speaker will I speak with him; in apparition, and not in similitudes; and he shall behold the likeness of the glory of the Lord. And how is this, that you have not been afraid to speak against My servant, against Mosheh?
12.9: And the displeasure of the Lord was strong against them, and He went up.
12.10: And the Cloud went up from over the tabernacle. And, behold, Miriam was white as snow; and Aharon looked upon Miriam, and, behold, she was leprous.
12.11: And Aharon said to Mosheh, My lord, I entreat that thou wouldst not lay this sin upon us, in that we have acted foolishly, and have transgressed.
12.12: Let not this one, I entreat, be separated from among us, for she is our sister. Pray, now, over this dead flesh which is in her, that she may be healed.
12.13: And Mosheh prayed before the Lord, saying: O God, I beseech Thee, heal her now.
12.14: But the Lord said to Mosheh, If her father, correcting, had corrected her, ought she not to have been ashamed seven days? Let her be shut up seven days without the camp, and afterward be admitted.
12.15: And Miriam was shut up without the camp seven days; and the people journeyed not until Miriam was brought in.
12.16: And afterward the people journeyed from Hatseroth, and encamped in the wilderness of Pharan.

13.1: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
13.2: Send thou men, that they may explore the land of Kenaan, which I will give to the children of Israel: one man for each tribe of their fathers shall you send, each one a ruler among them.
13.3: And Mosheh sent them from the wilderness of Pharan, according to the Word of the Lord. All those men were heads of the children of Israel;
13.4: And these are their names: For the tribe of Reuben, Shamua bar Zakur;
13.5: For the tribe of Shemeon, Shaphat bar Hori;
13.6: For the tribe of Jehudah, Kaleb bar Jephuneh;
13.7: For the tribe of Issakar, Igal bar Joseph;
13.8: For the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea bar Nun;
13.9: For the tribe of Benyamin, Phalti bar Raphu;
13.10: for the tribe of Zebulon, Gediel bar Sodi;
13.11: For the tribe of Joseph, the tribe of Menasheh, Gaddi bar Susi;
13.12: For the tribe of Dan, Ammiel bar GemaIi;
13.13: For the tribe of Asher, Sethor bar Mikael;
13.14: For the tribe of Naphtali, Nachbi bar Vapsi;
13.15: For the tribe of Gad, Geuel bar Machi:
13.16: These are the names of the men whom Mosheh sent to explore the land. And Mosheh called Hoshea bar Nun Jehoshua.
13.17: And Mosheh sent them away to explore the land of Kenaan. And he said to them, Go up hither by the south, and ascend to the mountain,
13.18: And see the country what it is, and the people who dwell upon it, whether they be strong or weak, few or many;
13.19: And what the land is in which they dwell, whether good or bad; and what the cities they inhabit, whether open, or walled in;
13.20: And whether the land is rich or poor; whether it hath trees or not: and you, be of good courage, and bring of the fruits of the land. And the days were the days of the first grapes.
13.21: And they went up, and explored the country, from the wilderness of Zin unto Rechob, to come unto Hamath.
13.22: And they went up by the south, and came to Hebron; and there were Achiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, sons of the giants; (and Hebron was built seven years before Tanis of Mizraim.)
13.23: And they came to the Stream of Grapes, and cut down there a branch, with one cluster of grapes, and carried it on a staff between two; and (they took also) of the pomegranates, and of the figs.
13.24: That place was called the Stream of Grapes, on account of the grapes (athkela) which the sons of Israel cut down from thence.
13.25: And they returned from the exploration of the country at the end of forty days.
13.26: And they went and came to Mosheh, and to Aharon, and to all the congregation of the children of Israel at the wilderness of Pharan, at Rekam, and returned the word to them, and to all the congregation, and showed them the fruit of the land.
13.27: And they recounted to him, and said: We came to the land whither thou didst send us, and truly it doth produce milk and honey, and this is the fruit of it.
13.28: But very mighty are the people who inhabit the land, and the cities are fortified and very great; and we saw, also, the sons of the giants there.
13.29: The Amalkaah dwell in the land of the south, and the Hittaah and Jebusaah and Amoraah dwell in the mountain, and the Kenaanaah dwell by the sea, and upon the bank of the Jordan.
13.30: And Kaleb quieted the people for Mosheh, and said: Going, let us go up and possess it, for we are able to (do) it:
13.31: But the men who had gone up with him said, We are not able to go up against the people, for they are stronger than we.
13.32: And they gave forth an evil report (name) about the land which they had explored to the children of Israel, saying: The country which we have passed through to search it, is a land that killeth its inhabitants;
13.33: And all the people whom we saw in it are men of stature; and there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, which are of the giants; and we looked, in our own sight, as locusts, and so were we in their eyes.

14.1: And all the congregation lifted up and gave (forth) their voice; and all the people wept that night.
14.2: And all the children of Israel murmured against Mosheh and Aharon; and the whole congregation said to them, O that we had died in the land of Mizraim, or that we had died in this wilderness!
14.3: And why is the Lord bringing us to this land, that we may fall by the sword, and our wives and our children become a prey? Would it not be better for us to return into Mizraim?
14.4: And they said, a man to his brother, Let us appoint a chieftain, and go back into Mizraim.
14.5: And Mosheh and Aharon fell upon their faces before all the assembly of the sons of Israel.
14.6: And Jehoshua bar Nun, and Kaleb bar Jephuneh, who were of the explorers of the land, rent their clothes.
14.7: And they spake to all the congregation of the sons of Israel, saying: The land, which we passed through to explore it, is a good land, most exceedingly.
14.8: If the Lord hath pleasure in us, even He will bring us into this land, and give us the land which produceth milk and honey.
14.9: Only be not rebellious against the Word of the Lord, nor be afraid of the people of the land, for they are delivered into our hand; their strength is departed from them, and the Word of the Lord is our helper: fear them not.
14.10: But all the congregation said that they would stone them with stones. And the Glory of the Lord was revealed at the tabernacle of ordinance, unto all the children of Israel.
14.11: And the Lord said to Mosheh, How long will this people provoke Me, and how long will they disbelieve in My Word, for all the signs which I have wrought among them?
14.12: I will smite them with the pestilence and consume them; and will make of thee a people greater and stronger than they.
14.13: But Mosheh said before the Lord, And the Mizraee will hear of it; for Thou didst bring up by Thy power this people from among them,
14.14: And they will tell unto the inhabitants of this land; for they have heard that Thou, O Lord, dost dwell in Thy Shekinah among this people, whose eyes behold the glorious Shekinah of the Lord, and that Thy Cloud overshadoweth them, and that in the pillar of the Cloud Thou conductest them in the day, and in the pillar of Fire by night.
14.15: Now if Thou shalt kill this people as one man, the nations who have heard the fame of Thy power will speak, saying:
14.16: Because there was not strength (enough) before the Lord to bring this people into the land which He covenanted to them, He hath killed them in the desert.
14.17: And now I beseech, let power be magnified from before the Lord, as Thou hast thus spoken, saying:
14.18: The Lord is far from anger, and great in performing goodness and truth: forgiving iniquity and rebellion and sins, pardoning them who return unto His law: but acquitting not them who will not, turn, (but) visiting the sins of the fathers upon the rebellious children unto the third and unto the fourth generation.
14.19: Pardon, I beseech, the sins of this people according to the amplitude of Thy goodness, and as Thou hast forgiven this people from Mizraim until now.
14.20: And the Lord said, I have pardoned according to thy word.
14.21: Yet, as I live, with the glory of the Lord shall all the earth be filled.
14.22: Because all these men who have seen My glory, and the signs I wrought in Mizraim and in the desert, but have tempted before Me these ten times, and have not been obedient to My Word,
14.23: if they shall see the land which I covenanted to their fathers, nor shall any see it who have provoked before Me.
14.24: But My servant Kaleb, for that there was in him another spirit, and that he hath wholly followed (in) My fear, him will I bring into the land whither he went, and his children shall possess it.
14.25: Now the Amalkaah and the Kenaanaah dwelt in the valley. Tomorrow, turn you and get you to the wilderness by the way of the Sea of Suph.
14.26: And the Lord spake with Mosheh and unto Aharon, saying:
14.27: How long shall this evil congregation be murmuring against Me? The murmuring of the sons of Israel which they murmur against Me is heard before Me.
14.28: Say to them, As I live, saith the Lord, even as ye have spoken before Me, so will I do to you.
14.29: In this wilderness shall your carcases fall, and all who are numbered of you, of all your numbers, from one of twenty years and upward who have murmured against me.
14.30: If you shall come into the land in which I covenanted in My Word to cause you to dwell, except Kaleb bar Jephuneh, and Jehoshua bar Nun.
14.31: But your children, of whom you said they were for a prey, will I bring in, and they shall know the land which you have abhorred.
14.32: But your carcases shall fall in this wilderness;
14.33: And your children shall go about in the wilderness forty years, and shall bear your iniquities until your carcases be laid in the wilderness.
14.34: According to the number of the days in which you explored the land, forty days, a day for a year, a day for a year, you shall receive for your sins, even forty years, and you shall know (the consequence of) your murmuring against me.
14.35: I, the Lord, have made the decree in My Word, if I will not do unto all this evil congregation who have gathered together against Me; in this wilderness shall they find their end, and here shall they die.
14.36: And the men whom Mosheh sent to search the land, and who returned to make all the congregation murmur against him, by bringing forth an evil name upon the land;
14.37: Those men who brought out the evil name upon the land died by the plague before the Lord.
14.38: But Jehoshua bar Nun and Kaleb bar Jephuneh lived, of those men who went to explore the land.
14.39: And Mosheh told these words to all the children of Israel, and the people bewailed greatly.
14.40: And they arose in the morning to go up to the top of the mountain, saying: Behold, we will go up to the place of which the Lord hath spoken; for we have sinned.
14.41: But Mosheh said, Wherefore do you transgress against the decree of the Word of the Lord? But it will not prosper.
14.42: Go not up, for the Shekinah of the Lord is not among you, and be not broken before your enemies.
14.43: For the Amalkaah and the Kenaanaah are there before you, and you will fall by the sword; for, because you have turned away from the service of the Lord, the Word of the Lord will not be your helper.
14.44: Yet they would commit the wickedness of going up to the summit of the mountain, though the ark of the Lord’s covenant, and Mosheh, removed not from the midst of the camp.
14.45: And the Amalkaah and the Kenaanaah who dwelt in the mountain came down and smote them, and pursued them unto Hormah.

15.1: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
15.2: Speak with the children of Israel, and say to them: When you shall (at last) have come into the land which I will give you,
15.3: and you will make an oblation before the Lord, a burnt offering, or a consecrated sacrifice for the release of a vow, or in a free-will offering, or in your solemnities to render an acceptable service before the Lord, from the herd or from the flock;
15.4: let him who offereth his oblation before the Lord bring for a mincha a tenth of flour sprinkled with the fourth of a hina of oil.
15.5: And wine for a libation the fourth of a hina shall he make upon the burnt offering, or hallowed sacrifice, for one lamb:
15.6: Or for a ram he shall make a mincha of two-tenths of flour sprinkled with the third of a hina of oil;
15.7: And wine for the libation thou shalt bring the third of a hina, to be received with acceptance before the Lord.
15.8: And when thou makest a bullock a burnt offering, or a hallowed sacrifice for the release of a vow, or hallowed sacrifices before the Lord,
15.9: let him bring with the bullock a mincha of three tenths of flour sprinkled with a half hina of oil;
15.10: And wine shalt thou bring for the libation the half of a hina, an oblation to be received with acceptance before the Lord.
15.11: So shalt thou do for one bullock, or one ram, or one lamb from the lambs, or from the kids.
15.12: According to the number that you perform so shall you do with each, according to their number.
15.13: All native-born (Hebrews) shall do these things to offer an oblation to be received with favour before the Lord.
15.14: And if a sojourner who sojourneth with you, or whoever among you in your generations will make an oblation to be received with favour before the Lord, as you do, so shall he do.
15.15: One congregation and one rite shall be for you and for the sojourners who sojourn; it is an everlasting statute; as you are, so shall the sojourner be before the Lord:
15.16: One law and one judgment shall be for you and for the sojourners who dwell with you.
15.17: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
15.18: Speak with the sons of Israel, and say to them, When you have come into the land into which I will bring you,
15.19: and when you eat of the bread of the land, you shall set apart a separation before the Lord.
15.20: Of the first of your food you shall set apart a cake for a separation; as the separation of the threshing-floor, so shall you set it apart;
15.21: Of the first of your bread (dough) you shall give the separation before the Lord in your generations.
15.22: And should you be in ignorance, and not do all these commandments of which the Lord hath spoken with Mosheh,
15.23: Even all which the Lord commanded you by the hand of Mosheh from the day that the Lord commanded and thenceforward in your generations,
15.24: It shall be that if anything be hid from the eyes of the congregation and you do ignorantly, then all the congregation shall make a burnt offering of one young bullock, to be received with acceptance before the Lord, with his mincha and his libation, according to the proper manner, and one kid of the goats for a sin offering:
15.25: And the priest shall make atonement for all the congregation of the sons of Israel, and it shall be forgiven them, for it was ignorance; but they shall bring their oblation before the Lord on account of their ignorance.
15.26: And it shall be forgiven to all the congregation of the children of Israel, and to the sojourners who sojourn among them; for all the people (were) in ignorance.
15.27: And if one sin ignorantly, he shall bring a female kid of the year for a sin offering;
15.28: And the priest shall make atonement for the man who hath erred in his sin through ignorance before the Lord, to atone for him, and it shall be forgiven him.
15.29: For the native-born of the sons of Israel, and for the sojourner who sojourneth among you, one law shall there be for you, for him who acteth in ignorance.
15.30: But the man who doeth presumptuously, whether of the native-born, or of the sojourners, he provoketh the Lord to anger, and that man shall perish from among his people:
15.31: Because he hath despised the word of the Lord, and hath made His commandment vain, that man shall be utterly destroyed, his sin is upon him.
15.32: And while the children of Israel were in the wilderness, they found a man stealing wood on the day of the Sabbath;
15.33: And they who had found him stealing wood brought him to Mosheh and Aharon, and to all the congregation.
15.34: And they bound him in the house of custody; for it had not been explained to them what they should do to him.
15.35: And the Lord said unto Mosheh, The man shall be surely put to death; all the congregation shall stone him with stones without the camp.
15.36: And all the congregation brought him forth without the camp, and stoned him with stones, and he died; as the Lord commanded Mosheh.
