15.37: And the Lord spake to Mosheh, saying:
15.38: Speak with the children of Israel, and bid them that they make them fringes upon the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and that upon the fringes on the borders they put a ribbon of hyacinth.
15.39: And they shall be to you for fringes, that you may look upon it, and remember all the commandments of the Lord, and do them, and not wander after the imagination of your heart, or after the sight of your eyes, after which you have gone astray.
15.40: That you may remember and do all My precepts, and be saints before your God.
15.41: I am the Lord your God who brought you forth from the land of Mizraim to be to you Eloha: I am the Lord your God.

16.1: But Korack bar zhar bar Kahath bar Levi, and Dathan and Abiram the sons of Eliab, and On bar Pelath of the Beni Reuben, made a division.
16.2: And they rose up in the presence of Mosheh with (other) men of the sons of Israel, two hundred and fifty, chiefs of the congregation, who at the time of the convocation had been men of name.
16.3: And they gathered together against Mosheh, and against Aharon, and said to them, You are too great; for the whole of the congregation are all of them holy, and the Lord’s Shekinah dwelleth among them: wherefore then are you lifted up above the church (congregation) of the Lord?
16.4: And Mosheh heard, and fell upon his face.
16.5: And he spake with Korach, and with all the congregation, saying: In the morning the Lord will make blown who it is who pertaineth to Him, and who bath been consecrated to approach to His presence; and whosoever He shall appoint shall go near unto His service.
16.6: This do: Take you censers, Korach and all his congregation;
16.7: And put fire in them, and put sweet incense upon it before the Lord tomorrow: and the man whom the Lord will choose, he shall be holy. You have too much, sons of Levi.
16.8: And Mosheh said to Korach, Hear now, sons of Levi:
16.9: Is it a little thing with you that the God of Israel hath separated you from the congregation of Israel to bring you near before Him to perform the service of the Lord’s tabernacle, and to stand before the congregation to minister to them?
16.10: But He hath brought thee nigh, and all thy brethren the sons of Levi with thee: and seek you now the High Priesthood also?
16.11: Therefore thou and all thy company have gathered together against the Lord. And Aharon, what is he, that you murmur against him?
16.12: And Mosheh, sent to call Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab; but they said, We will not come up.
16.13: Is it a trifle that thou hast brought us from a land making milk and honey to kill us in the desert, that thou mayest domineer and rule over us?
16.14: Neither hast thou brought us into the land that maketh milk and honey, to give us an inheritance of fields and vineyards: wilt thou blind the eyes of these men? We will not come up.
16.15: And Mosheh was greatly angered, and said before the Lord, Receive not Thou their offering: I have not taken one ass from them, neither have I injured one of them.
16.16: And Mosheh said to Korach, Be thou and all thy company prepared before the Lord, thou and they and Aharon tomorrow.
16.17: And take every man his censer, and put sweet incense upon them, each man to offer before the Lord (with) his censer.
16.18: And they took every man his censer, and set fire in it, and put sweet incense thereon, and stood at the door of the tabernacle of ordinance, with Mosheh and Aharon.
16.19: And Korach assembled with him all the company at the door of the tabernacle of ordinance. And the glory of the Lord was revealed to all the congregation.
16.20: And the Lord spake with Mosheh and to Aharon, saying:
16.21: Separate yourselves from among this company, and I will consume them at once.
16.22: But they fell upon their faces, and said, O God, the God of the spirits of all flesh, shall one man sin, and thou be wroth with all the congregation?
16.23: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
16.24: Speak with the congregation, saying: Get you up from among the tents of Korach, Dathan, and Abiram.
16.25: And Mosheh arose and went unto Dathan and Abiram, and the elders of Israel followed him.
16.26: And he spake with the congregation, saying: Remove now from the tents of these guilty men, and touch not anything that is theirs, lest you be stricken with all their sins.
16.27: And they gat up from the tents of Korach, Dathan, and Abiram round about; and Dathan and Abiram came out, and stood at the door of their tents, with their wives, and their sons, and their families.
16.28: And Mosheh said: By this shall you know that the Lord hath sent me to do all these works, because (I do them) not of my own will:
16.29: If these men die the death of all men, and the visitation of all men be visited upon them, the Lord hath not sent me.
16.30: But if the Lord create a creation, and the earth open her mouth, and swallow them up, and all that is theirs, and they go down alive into Sheul, then you will know that these men have caused anger before the Lord.
16.31: And it was, when he had finished to speak all these words, that the ground under them clave asunder,
16.32: and the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed them up, and the men of their houses; and all the men of Korach, and all their substance,
16.33: they, and all who were theirs, went down alive into Sheul; and the earth closed upon them, and they perished from among the congregation.
16.34: And all Israel who stood round about them fled from their cry; for they said, Lest the earth swallow us.
16.35: And fire came out from before the Lord, and consumed the two hundred and fifty men who had offered the sweet incense.

17.1: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
17.2: Speak to Elazar bar Aharon the priest, that he take out the censers from among the burnings, and throwaway the fire, for they are consecrated.
17.3: The censers of those guilty men who sinned against their souls, let him make of them beaten plates, to cover the altar; for they had offered them before the Lord, and they are consecrated; and they shall be for a sign unto the children of Israel.
17.4: And Elazar the priest took the golden censers, with which they who were burned had offered, and beat them abroad, for a covering for the altar,
17.5: to be a memorial to the sons of Israel, that no strange man who is not of the seed of Aharon shall approach to burn sweet incense before the Lord, and that he be not as Korach and his company, as the Lord had said to him by the hand of Mosheh.
17.6: But on the day which followed, all the congregation of the sons of Israel murmured against Mosheh and against Aharon, saying: You have caused the death of the Lord’s people.
17.7: And it was, while the congregation gathered against Mosheh and against Aharon, that they looked toward the tabernacle of ordinance; and, behold, the cloud covered it, and the glory of the Lord was revealed.
17.8: And Mosheh and Aharon went up before the tabernacle of ordinance;
17.9: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
17.10: separate yourselves from the midst of this congregation, that I may now consume them. But they fell upon their faces.
17.11: And Mosheh said to Aharon: Take the censer, and put fire upon it from the altar, and lay on sweet incense, and go quickly to the congregation, and make atonement for them; for anger hath gone forth from before the Lord, the plague hath begun.
17.12: And Aharon took, as Mosheh had said, and ran into the midst of the congregation, and, behold, the plague had begun among the people; and he put on sweet incense and made atonement for the people.
17.13: And he stood between the dead and the living, and the plague ceased.
17.14: But they who died of the plague were fourteen thousand and seven hundred, beside those who died on account of the matter of Korach.
17.15: And Aharon returned to Mosheh, unto the door of the tabernacle of ordinance, and the plague ceased.
17.16: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
17.17: Speak with the sons of Israel, and take from them severally a rod, according the house of their fathers, twelve rods, and write thou the name of each man upon his rod.
17.18: And upon the rod of Levi thou shalt write the name of Aharon; for one rod (only) there shall be for each chief of their father’s house.
17.19: And thou shalt lay them up in the tabernacle of ordinance before the testimony, where I will appoint My Word to be with thee.
17.20: And it shall be that the rod of the man whom I will choose shall bud; and I will make to cease from before Me the murmuring; of the sons of Israel, with which they have murmured against you.
17.21: And Mosheh spake with the sons of Israel; and all their chiefs gave to him, every chief one rod, according to the house of their fathers, twelve rods. And Aharon’s rod was among their rods.
17.22: And Mosheh laid up the rods before the Lord in the tabernacle of the testimony.
17.23: And it came to pass on the following day, that Mosheh went into the tabernacle of the testimony; and, behold, the rod of Aharon of the house of Levi had germinated, and produced branches, and had blossomed, and ripened almonds.
17.24: And Mosheh brought out all the rods from before the Lord unto all the sons of Israel, and they recognized and took every man his rod.
17.25: And the Lord said to Mosheh: Take back Aharon’s rod before the testimony, to be kept for a sign unto the rebellious people, that their murmurings before Me may come to an end, and they die not.
17.26: And Mosheh did as the Lord commanded, so did he.
17.27: And the children of Israel spake to Mosheh, saying: Behold, some of us are slain with the sword; and, behold, some are swallowed up by the earth; and, behold, some perish with the plague.
17.28: Whoever, approaching, approacheth the tabernacle of the Lord dieth; behold, we are consumed with death.

18.1: And the Lord said to Aharon: Thou and thy sons, and the house of thy fathers with thee, shall make reconciliation on account of transgressions (against) the sanctuary; and thou and thy sons with thee shall make atonement for the sins of your priesthood.
18.2: And thy brethren also of the tribe of Levi, the tribe of thy father, bring with thee, and let them be added with thee, to serve thee; but thou and, thy sons with thee (shall minister) before the tabernacle of the testimony.
18.3: And they shall keep thy charge, and the charge of all the tabernacle; but to the vessels of the sanctuary and of the altar they (the Levites) shall not approach, that neither they nor you may die.
18.4: And they shall be joined, with thee, and keep charge of the tabernacle of ordinance for all the service of the tabernacle, and a stranger shall not come near you.
18.5: And they shall keep charge of the sanctuary and of the altar, that there may be no more wrath upon the sons of Israel.
18.6: And, behold, I have taken your brethren, the Levites, from among the sons of Israel; as a gift are they given to you before the Lord, to perform the service of the tabernacle of ordinance.
18.7: But thou, and thy sons with thee, take charge of your priesthood, for everything about the altar and within the veil you shall fulfil the service; the ministry of the priesthood I have given you as a gift, and the stranger who cometh near shall die.
18.8: And the Lord said to Aharon: Behold, I have given to thee the charge of My separated things; of all that are consecrated by the sons of Israel unto thee have I given them, and to thy sons, on account of the anointing, by an everlasting statute.
18.9: This shall be thine of the most holy things which remain from the fire, of all their oblations, and of all their minchas, and of all their sin offerings, and of all their trespass offerings which they render before Me; they are most sacred to thee and to thy sons.
18.10: In the sanctuary thou mayest eat thereof, every male may eat it, to thee it shall be consecrated.
18.11: And this is thine: the separated things of their minchas, of all the elevations of the sons of Israel, to thee have I given them, and to thy sons, and to thy daughters with thee, by an everlasting statute: everyone who is clean in thy house may eat thereof.
18.12: All the best of the oil, and all the best of the wine, and the wheat, the firstfruits of them which they present before the Lord, unto thee I have given them.
18.13: The firstfruits of all that is on their land which they present before the Lord shall be thine; everyone in thy house who is clean may eat thereof.
18.14: Everything devoted in Israel shall be thine.
18.15: Whatever openeth the womb of all flesh which they offer before the Lord, of man, or of beast, shall be for thee; but thou shalt surely redeem the firstborn of man, and the firstling of an unclean animal thou shalt redeem;
18.16: And his redemption shall be at the age of one month; thou shalt redeem with the price of five shekes, in the shekel of the sanctuary it is ten meahs:
18.17: But the firstling of an ox, or of a sheep, or of a goat, thou mayest not redeem, they are consecrated; thou shalt sprinkle their blood upon the altar, and burn their fat, an oblation to be accepted before the Lord.
18.18: But their flesh shall be for thee, as the breast of the elevation, and the right shoulder, they shall be thine.
18.19: All the consecrated separations which the sons of Israel set apart before the Lord, I have given to thee and to thy children with thee by an everlasting covenant; an everlasting covenant of salt it is before the Lord, with thee, and thy children with thee.
18.20: And the Lord said to Aharon: In their land thou wilt not have possession, nor will thine be a portion among them; the gifts that I have given thee, they are thy portion and thy inheritance among the children of Israel.
18.21: And to the sons of Levi, behold, I have given all the tenths in Israel for a possession, on account of the service with which they serve in the ministry of the tabernacle of ordinance.
18.22: But the children of Israel must no more come nigh to the tabernacle of ordinance, to contract guilt and to die.
18.23: But the Levites shall perform the service of the tabernacle of ordinance, and shall bear their iniquity; a statute forever unto your generations. And among the sons of Israel they shall not possess an inheritance;
18.24: For the tenths of the children of Israel which they set apart before the Lord for a separation, I have given to the Levites for a possession; therefore have I said to them, Among the sons of Israel you shall not possess an inheritance.
18.25: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
18.26: Speak also to the Levites, and say to them, When you take from the sons of Israel the tenths which I have given you of theirs, you shall set apart from them a separation before the Lord, a tenth of the tenth.
18.27: And your separation shall be reckoned to you as the corn from the threshing-floor, and as the wine of the wine-press;
18.28: So shall you set apart the separation before the Lord of all your tenths that you receive from the sons of Israel, and give thereof a separation before the Lord unto Aharon the priest.
18.29: Of all that is given to you ye shall set apart every separation for the Lord, of all the best of it, to be the hallowed portion thereof.
18.30: And say thou to them, When you have set apart the finest of it, it shall be reckoned to the Levites as the produce of the threshing-floor, and as the fruitage for the wine-press;
18.31: And you may eat it in every place, you and the men of your house; for it is a remuneration to you on account of your service in the tabernacle of ordinance.
18.32: And you shall not contract guilt by it in your setting apart the finest of it, nor profane the consecrated things of the children of Israel.

19.1: And the Lord spake with Mosheh and to Aharon, saying:
19.2: This is the decree of the law which the Lord hath commanded, saying: Speak to the sons of Israel that they bring to thee a red heifer, unblemished, with no spot in her, and upon which no yoke hath been put.
19.3: And you shall give her unto Elazar the priest, that he may bring her without the camp, and (one) shall slaughter her before him.
19.4: And Elazar, the priest, shall take (some) of her blood with his finger, and sprinkle of her blood against the face of the tabernacle of ordinance seven times.
19.5: And (one) shall burn the heifer before his eyes; her skin, and her flesh, and her blood, with her food shall he burn.
19.6: And the priest shall take cedar wood, and hyssop, and scarlet, and cast it into the midst of the burning of the heifer.
19.7: And the priest shall wash his clothes, and bathe his flesh in water, and afterwards come into the camp: but the priest shall be unclean until the evening.
19.8: And he who burneth her shall wash his clothes with water, and bathe his flesh in water, and be unclean until evening.
19.9: And a man who is clean shall gather up the ashes of the heifer, and lay them up without the camp in a clean place, and it shall be for the congregation of the children of Israel to keep, for the sprinkling with water; it is (a purification) for sin.
19.10: And he who gathereth up the ashes of the heifer shall wash his raiment, and be unclean until the evening; and it shall be for the children of Israel, and for the strangers who dwell among you, a statute forever.
19.11: Whosoever toucheth the dead of any of mankind shall be unclean seven days.
19.12: He shall sprinkle with it on the third day, and on the seventh day shall be clean; but if he sprinkle it not on the third day, on the seventh day he shall not be clean.
19.13: Whoever toucheth the dead body of a man who hath died, and sprinkleth not with it, defileth the tabernacle of the Lord; and that man shall be cut off from Israel: because the water of sprinkling is not sprinkled upon him, he shall be unclean, (for) his uncleanness is yet upon him.
19.14: This is the law when a man dieth in a tent: everyone who entereth the tent, and everyone who is in the tent, shall be unclean seven days.
19.15: And every open earthen vessel which hath not a covering fastened upon it round about is unclean.
19.16: And whoever toucheth one who is slain with the sword upon the face of the field, or a dead body, or the bone of a man, or a grave, shall be unclean seven days.
19.17: And for the unclean person they shall take of the ashes of the burnt sin offering, and put spring water upon it in a vessel.
19.18: And a man who is clean shall take hyssop, and dip it in the water, and sprinkle upon the tent, and upon every vessel, and upon the persons who are there, and upon him who had touched the bone, or the slain, or the dead body, or the grave.
19.19: And the clean person shall sprinkle the unclean on the third day, and on the seventh day; and on the seventh day he shall be clean; and shall sprinkle his raiment, and wash with water, and at the evening he shall be clean.
19.20: But the man who is unclean, and it bath not been sprinkled upon him, shall be cut off from the congregation, because he would defile the sanctuary of the Lord. The water of sprinkling was not sprinkled upon him; he is unclean.
19.21: And it shall be to them for an everlasting statute, that he who applieth the water of sprinkling shall wash his clothes, and whoever toucheth the water of sprinkling shall be unclean until the evening;
19.22: And whatever may be touched by the unclean person shall be unclean, and the man who toucheth it shall be unclean until the evening.

20.1: And the children of Israel, the whole congregation, came to the wilderness of Zin in the first month, and the people abode in Rekem; and Miriam died there, and was buried there.
20.2: And there was no water for the congregation; and they gathered against Mosheh and against Aharon;
20.3: And the people were contentious with Mosheh, and spake, saying, Would that we had died when our brethren died before the Lord!
20.4: And why have you brought the congregation of the Lord into this wilderness, that we and our cattle may die here?
20.5: And wherefore have you made us come up from Mizraim, to bring us into this evil place? This is not a place for sowing; here are neither fig trees, nor vines, nor pomegranates, neither is there water to drink.
20.6: And Mosheh and Aharon went up from before the congregation unto the door of the tabernacle of ordinance, and fell upon their faces; and the glory of the Lord was revealed to them.
20.7: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying,
20.8: Take the rod, and gather the congregation together, thou and Aharon thy brother, and speak to the Rock, before their eyes, and it shall give its waters; and thou shalt bring forth water for them from the rock, and give drink to the congregation and their cattle.
20.9: And Mosheh took the rod from before the Lord, as He had commanded him.
20.10: And Mosheh and Aharon assembled the congregation before the rock; and he said to them: Hear now, rebels! Are we to draw forth water for you from this rock?
20.11: And Mosheh lifted up his hand, and smote the rock with the rod two times; and the waters came forth greatly, and the congregation drank and their cattle.
20.12: But the Lord spake unto Mosheh and Aharon: Because you have not believed in My Word to sanctify Me in the eyes of the sons of Israel, therefore you shall not bring this congregation into the land that I have given them.
20.13: These are the Waters of Strife, because the sons of Israel strove before the Lord, and He was sanctified in them.
20.14: And Mosheh sent ambassadors from Rekem to the king of Edom: Thus saith thy brother Israel, Thou knowest all the trouble we have found;
20.15: That our fathers went down into Mizraim, and we dwelt in Mizraim many days, and the Mizraee badly treated us and our fathers.
20.16: And we prayed before the Lord, and He accepted our prayers, and sent an Angel, and brought us out from Mizraim; and, behold, we are in Rekem, a city which is on the side of thy border.
20.17: Let us now pass through thy country: we will not go through a field or through a vineyard, nor will we drink up the water of the cistern: on the king’s highway will we travel; we will not turn to the right hand or to the left until we have passed through thy border
20.18: But Edomea said to him, Thou shalt not pass through my border, lest I come out against thee with the slaughtering sword.
20.19: And the sons of Israel said to him, We would go up by the trodden way; and if we drink of thy water, I and my cattle, we will give thee the price of it; we will do nothing evil; upon my feet I will pass through.
20.20: But he said, Thou shalt not pass through. And Edomea came out to meet him with great force and with a strong hand.
20.21: So Edomea refused to permit Israel to go through his border; and Israel turned away from him.
20.22: And they went forward from Rekem, and all the congregation of the children of Israel came to Mount Hor.
20.23: And the Lord spake to Mosheh and to Aharon at Mount Hor, by the coast of the land of Edom, saying:
20.24: Aharon shall be gathered unto his people; for he shall not enter into the land which I have given to the children of Israel, because you rebelled against My Word at the waters of strife.
20.25: Take Aharon and Elazar his son, and bring them up to Mount Hor;
20.26: And strip Aharon of his vestments, and put them upon Elazar his son; and Aharon shall be gathered (to his people), and shall die there.
20.27: And Mosheh did as the Lord commanded, and they went up to Mount Hor before the eyes of all the congregation.
20.28: And Mosheh took off his garments from Aharon, and put them upon Elazar his son. And Aharon died there, on the summit of the mount. And Mosheh and Elazar came down from the mount.
20.29: And all the congregation saw that Aharon was dead; and all the house of Israel bewailed Aharon thirty days.

21.1: And when the Kenaanah, king Arad, who dwelt in the south, heard that Israel was coming by the way of the explorers, he set battle in array against Israel, and took some of them captives.
21.2: And Israel vowed a vow before the Lord, and said: If Thou wilt surely deliver this people into my hand, then I will destroy their cities.
21.3: And the Lord accepted Israel’s prayer, and gave up the Kenaanaah; and he destroyed them and their cities, and he called the name of the place Charma.
21.4: And they journeyed from Mount Hor by the way of the Sea of Suph, to go round from the land of Edom: and the soul of the people was wearied in the way.
21.5: And the people murmured (or, growled) against the Word of the Lord, and contended with Mosheh, (saying) Why have you brought us up out of Mizraim to die in the desert? For there is neither bread nor water, and our soul is weary of manna, this light food.
21.6: And the Lord sent forth burning serpents among the people, and much people of Israel died.
21.7: And the people came to Mosheh, and said: We have sinned, for we have murmured before the Lord, and have contended with thee. Intercede before the Lord, that He may remove the serpents from among us. And Mosheh prayed for the people.
21.8: And the Lord said to Mosheh: Make thee a burning (serpent), and uplift it on an ensign; and everyone who hath been bitten, and beholdeth it, shall live (or, be saved).
21.9: And Mosheh made a serpent of brass, and set it upon an ensign; and when a serpent had bitten a man, if he looked up to the serpent of brass, he lived (or, was saved).
21.10: And the children of Israel journeyed and encamped in Oboth.
21.11: And they journeyed from Oboth, and encamped at the Ford of the Passengers, which is in the wilderness over against Moab, toward the sunrise.
21.12: And they removed from thence, and encamped by the brook Zared.
21.13: Thence they journeyed, and pitched on the other side of Arnon, that is in the wilderness that stretcheth out from the coasts of the Amoraah; for Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amoraah.
21.14: Wherefore it is said in the Book of the Wars, That which the Lord did by the Sea of Suph, and the great deeds which (He wrought) by the torrents of Arnon,
21.15: And at the flowing of the streams which lead towards Lechayath, and are joined at the confine of Moab.
21.16: And from thence was given to them the well, which is the well whereof the Lord spake to Mosheh, Gather the people together, and I will give them water.
21.17: Therefore sang Israel this song: Spring up, O well; sing ye unto it.
21.18: The well which the princes digged, the chiefs of the people cut it, the scribes with their staves; it was given to them in the wilderness.
21.19: And from (the time) that it was given to them it descended with them to the rivers, and from the rivers it went up with them to the height,
21.20: And from the height to the vale which is in the fields of Moab, at the head of Ramatha, which looketh towards Beth Jeshimon.
21.21: And Israel sent messengers to Sihon, king of the Amoraah, saying:
21.22: I would pass through thy country: I will not turn aside into field or vineyard; we will not drink of the waters of the cistern; by the king’s highway will we go until we have crossed thy border.
21.23: But Sihon would not permit Israel to pass through his coast; and Sihon gathered all his people, and came out to prevent Israel in the wilderness, and came to Jahaz, and arrayed battle against Israel.
21.24: And Israel smote him with the edge of the sword, and took possession of his land from Arnon unto Jabbok, unto the Beni Ammon; for the border of the Beni Ammon was strong.
21.25: And Israel subdued all those cities, and Israel dwelt in all the cities of the Amoraah, in Heshbon, and in all the villages thereof.
21.26: For Heshbon was the city of Sihon, king of the Amoraah; he had made war with the former king of Moab, and had taken all his territory from his hand unto Arnon.
21.27: Therefore, say the proverbs: Come to Heshbon; let the city of Sihon be builded and finished:
21.28: For an east wind strong as fire hath gone out from Heshbon, and the servants of war (as) with a flame from the city of Sihon: they have slain the people who inhabited Lechayath of Moab, the priests who ministered in the idol-temple in the height of Arnona.
21.29: Woe to you, Moabaee, you are undone, ye people who have worshipped Kemosh; he hath delivered up his besieged sons and his daughters into captivity, unto Sihon, king of the Amoraah.
21.30: And the kingdom hath ceased from Heshbon, the dominion hath passed away from Dibon, they have laid waste unto Nophak which joineth Medeba.
21.31: And Israel dwelt in the land of the Amoraah.
21.32: And Mosheh sent to explore Jaazer; and they subdued the towns, and drave out the Amoraah who were therein.
21.33: And they turned and went up by the way of Mathnan; and Og, king of Mathnan, came out to meet them, he and all his people, to give battle at Edrei.
21.34: But the Lord said to Mosheh, Fear him not: for I have delivered him into thy hand with all his people and his country; and thou shalt do to him as thou hast done to Sihon, the king of the Amoraah who dwelt in Heshbon.
21.35: And they smote him, and his sons, and all his people, until none remained of him who were spared; and they took possession of his land.

22.1: And the sons of Israel moved onward, and encamped in the plain of Moab (at some space) from the ford of the Jordan (towards) Jericho.
22.2: And Balak bar Zippor saw all that Israel had done to the Amoraah.
22.3: And the Moabaah feared before the people greatly, because they were many; yea, the Moabaee were in distress before the sons of Israel.
22.4: And Moab said to the elders of Midian, Now will this host consume all that are round about us, as the ox licketh up the herbage of the field. And Balak bar Zippor was the king of Moab at that time.
22.5: And he sent messengers to Bileam bar Beor unto Pethor Aram which is upon the Phrat, the land of the sons of his people, to call him, saying: Behold, a people hath come out of Mizraim; lo, they cover the sunshine from the earth, and they are dwelling over against me.
22.6: Come now, I entreat, curse this people for me, for they are stronger than I: if perhaps I may become able to fight with him, and drive him from the land: for I know that he whom thou blessest is blessed, and he whom thou dost curse is accursed.
22.7: And the elders of Moab and of Midian went, with the (price of) divinations in their hands, and came to Bileam, and told him the words of Balak.
22.8: And he said to them, Lodge here for the night, and I will return you word, according as the Lord speaketh with me. And the princes of Moab tarried with Bileam.
22.9: And a word from before the Lord came unto Bileam, and said, Who are these men who are with thee?
22.10: And Bileam said before the Lord, Balak bar Zippor, king of Moab, hath sent to me.
22.11: Behold, a people are come out of Mizraim, and hide the glance of the sun from the earth. Now come, curse him for me, that I may be able to fight him, and drive him away.
22.12: And the Lord said to Bileam, Thou shalt not go with them: thou shalt not curse the people, for he is blessed.
22.13: And Bileam arose in the morning, and said to the princes of Balak, Go back to your country; for it is not pleasing before the Lord to permit me to go with you.
22.14: And the princes of Moab arose and came to Balak, and said, Bileam refuseth to come with us.
22.15: But Balak added to send princes more (in number) and nobler than those.
22.16: And they came to Bileam, and said to him: Thus saith Balak bar Zippor: Be not, I beseech thee, hindered from coming to me;
22.17: For I will greatly honour thee with honour, and will do all that thou shalt bid me. Come, then, curse me this people.
22.18: Bileam responded, and said to the servants of Balak: If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I have no power to transgress the decree of the Word of the Lord my God, to do either little or great.
22.19: But now I beg you tarry here this night, that I may know what yet the Lord will speak unto me.
22.20: And word came from before the Lord unto Bileam by night, and said to him: If the men come to call thee, arise and go with them; nevertheless the word that I speak with thee, that thou shalt do.
22.21: And Bileam rose up in the morning, and saddled his ass, and went with the princes of Moab.
22.22: But the displeasure of the Lord was provoked because he (so) went; and the angel of the Lord stood in the road to withstand him: and he was riding upon his ass, and his two young men with him.
22.23: And the ass discerned the angel of the Lord standing in the way with his sword drawn in his hand; and the ass started aside from the road, and went into the field. And Bileam struck the ass to make her to return into the road.
22.24: And the angel of the Lord (again) stood in the way of the vineyards in a place where there was a fence here and a fence there.
22.25: And the ass discerned the angel of the Lord, and thrust herself to the wall, and drave Bileam’s foot against the wall; and he smote her again.
22.26: And the angel of the Lord yet passed on, and stood in a narrow place where there was no way to turn to the right or to the left.
22.27: And the ass discerned the angel of the Lord, and fell down under Bileam; and Bileam’s wrath was provoked, and he smote the ass with his staff.
22.28: And the Lord opened the mouth of the ass; and she spake to Bileam, What have I done to thee that thou bast smitten me these three times?
22.29: And Bileam said to the ass, Because thou hast mocked me: would that there was a sword in my hand! For now would I kill thee.
22.30: And the ass said to Bileam, Am I not thy ass, upon whom thou hast ridden from (the time that) I have been thine unto this day? Have I ever been used to do thus to thee? And he said, No.
22.31: And the Lord unveiled Bileam’s eyes, and he saw the angel of the Lord standing in the road with his sword unsheathed in his hand: and he bowed, and worshipped upon his face.
22.32: And the angel of the Lord said to him, Wherefore hast thou smitten thine ass these three times? Behold, I have come out to withstand thee, because it is seen before me that thou art willing to go in a way contrary to me.
22.33: But the ass discerned me, and turned from before me these three times: unless she had turned from before me, now should I have slain thee, and her would I have spared.
22.34: And Bileam said to the angel of the Lord, I knew not that thou wast standing before me in the way. And now, if it be evil in thine eyes, I will return.
22.35: But the angel of the Lord said to Bileam, Go with the men; only the word that I shall speak with thee, that thou shalt say. And Bileam went with the princes of Balak.
22.36: And Balak heard that Bileam was coming, and went forth to meet him, at a city of Moab which is upon the border of Arnon, on the side of the frontier.
22.37: And Balak said to Bileam, Did not I sending send for thee to call thee? Why didst thou not come to me? Hast thou not indeed said that I am not able to do thee honour?
22.38: And Bileam said to Balak, Behold, I have come to thee: but even now, have’ I really any power to speak anything? The word which the Lord putteth into my mouth I will speak.
22.39: And Bileam went with Balak, and they came to a city of his territory.
22.40: And Balak slaughtered oxen and sheep, and sent to Bileam and to the princes who were with him.
22.41: And when it was morning, Balak took Bileam, and brought him up to the high places of his idol; and he saw from thence the extreme of the people.

23.1: And Bileam said to Balak, Build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven bullocks and seven rams.
23.2: And Balak did as Bileam had spoken, and Balak and Bileam offered up a bullock and a ram upon every altar.
23.3: And Bileam said to Balak, Remain by thy burnt offering; and I will go, if perhaps the Word may meet me from before the Lord; and the word that He showeth me I will disclose unto thee. And he went solitary.
23.4: And the Word from before the Lord met Bileam; and he said to Him; The seven altars have I set in order, and have offered a bullock and a ram upon every altar.
23.5: And the Lord put a word upon Bileam’s mouth, and said to him: Return unto Balak, and thus shalt thou speak.
23.6: And he returned to him, and, behold, he was standing by his burnt sacrifice, he and all the nobles of Moab.
23.7: And he took up his parable, and said: Balak, king of Moab, hath brought me from Aram, From the mountains of the east: Come, curse me, Jakob, Come, hunt down Israel for me.
23.8: How shall I curse whom God hath not cursed? How shall I persecute whom God hath not?
23.9: For from the top of the mountain I discern him, And look upon him from the heights; Lo, the people by themselves are to possess the world, And among the nations they shall not be judged with consumption.
23.10: Who can number the dust of the house of Jakob, Of whom it is said, They shall increase as the dust of the earth, Or of one of the four camps of Israel? Let mine be the death of his truthful ones, And let my end be as theirs!
23.11: And Balak said to Bileam, What hast thou done to me? I brought thee to curse my enemies, and, behold, blessing hast thou blessed them.
23.12: But he said, That which the Lord hath put in my mouth must I not observe to speak?
23.13: And Balak said to him, Come now with me to another place, from whence thou mayest see him, where thou canst see only the outer side, but not the whole, and curse him for me from thence.
23.14: And he brought him to the field of the watch-tower on the top of the hill; and builded seven altars, and offered a bullock and a ram on every altar.
23.15: And he said to Balak, Stand here by thy burnt offering, and I will go yonder.
23.16: And the Word from before the Lord met Bileam, and put a word in his mouth, and said, Return to Balak, and thus speak.
23.17: And he came to him, and he was standing by his burnt offering, and the nobles of Moab with him. And Balak said to him, What hath the Lord spoken?
23.18: And he took up his parable, and said: Arise, Balak, and hear, Listen to my words, Bar Zippor:
23.19: The word of Eloha is not as the words of men; The sons of men speak, but lie; Nor is it as the works of the children of flesh, Who decree to do, but repent, and change their counsels. What He hath said He will perform, And His every word is steadfast.
23.20: Behold, I have received benedictions to bless Israel, And I may not turn my blessing from him.
23.21: I have seen that in the house of Jakob The worshippers of idols are not, Nor in Israel the workers of the work of lies. The Word of the Lord their God is their helper, And the Shekinah of their King is among them.
23.22: God, who brought them out from Mizraim, Becomes his strength and exaltation.
23.23: For no divinations can prosper against the house of Jakob, Nor enchantments against the myriads of Israel. According to the time it shall be said of Jakob and of Israel, What hath Eloah wrought!
23.24: Behold, the people shall dwell as a lioness, And as a lion shall he lift himself up; Until he hath slain with slaughter, He will not rest in his land, And inherit the treasures of the nations.
23.25: And Balak said to Bileam, Neither cursing curse them, nor blessing bless them.
23.26: But Bileam answered and said to Balak, Did I not tell thee, saying, All that the Lord speaketh, that I must do?
23.27: And Balak said to Bileam, Come now, I will take thee to another place; perhaps it may be pleasing before the Lord, that thou mayest curse them for me from thence.
23.28: And Balak conducted Bileam to the top of the high place that looketh toward the face of Beth Jeshimon.
23.29: And Bileam said to Balak, Build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven bullocks and seven rams.
23.30: And Balak did as Bileam had said, and offered a bullock and a ram on every altar.

24.1: And Bileam saw that it was appointed before the Lord to bless Israel; and he went not as at those former times to inquire by divinations, but set his face towards the calf that the sons of Israel had made in the wilderness.
24.2: And Bileam lifted up his eyes, and beheld Israel dwelling by his tribes; and the Spirit of prophecy rested upon him from before the Lord.
24.3: And he took up his parable, and said: Bileam, the son of Beor, hath said, The man who saw the Beautiful hath said,
24.4: he hath said who heard the Word from before God, Who saw the vision of the Almighty, prostrate when he saw:
24.5: How goodly is thy land, O Jakob, And the house of thy habitation, O Israel!
24.6: As rivers flowing onward; as the watered garden by Euphrates, As aromatics planted by the Lord; as cedars planted by the waters.
24.7: The king anointed from his sons shall increase, And have dominion over many nations; His king shall be mightier than Agag, and his kingdom be exalted.
24.8: God, who brought them from Mizraim, is mighty and high, and by Him Shall Israel use the wealth of the nations their foes, Enjoy the spoils of their kings, and inherit their lands.
24.9: He reposed in his strength, as the lion and the lioness, And no kingdom may commove him. They who bless thee shall be blessed, And they who curse thee be accursed.
24.10: And the anger of Balak was roused against Bileam, and he smote his hands together. And Balak said to Bileam, I called thee to curse my enemies, and, behold, blessing hast thou blessed them these three times!
24.11: And now go to thy place. I said, Honouring I would honour thee; but, behold, the Lord hath kept thee back from honour.
24.12: But Bileam said to Balak, Did I not also tell the messengers whom thou sentest to me, saying,
24.13: If Balak would give me his house full of silver and gold, I have no power to transgress the decree of the Word of the Lord, to do good or evil of my own will; whatsoever the Lord shall sat that will I speak?
24.14: And now, behold, I go unto my people. Come, I will give thee counsel what thou shouldst do; and will show thee what this people will do unto thy people at the end of the days.
24.15: And he took up his parable, and said: Bileam, the son of Beor, speaketh, The man who saw the Beautiful speaketh,
24.16: He speaks who heard the Word from before God, And who knoweth knowledge from the Most High, Who saw the vision of the Almighty, prostrate when he saw.
24.17: I see him, but not now; I behold him, but not nigh. When a king shall arise out of Jakob, And the Meshiha be anointed from Israel, He will slay the princes of Moab, and reign over all the children of men;
24.18: And Edom shall be an inheritance, And Seir a possession of his adversaries; But Israel shall prosper in riches.
24.19: One will descend from the house of Jakob, Who will destroy him that escapeth from the city of the peoples.
24.20: And he looked on the Amalkaah, and took up his parable, and said: Amalek was the beginning of the wars of Israel, But in his end he shall perish forever.
24.21: And he beheld the Shalmaah, and took up his parable, and said: Strong is the house of thy dwelling, And in a strong fortress thou hast set thy abode;
24.22: But yet Shalmaah shall be destroyed, For Athuria will make thee captive.
24.23: And he took up his parable, and said: Woe to the wicked who may live when God doeth this!
24.24: And ships will come from the Kittaee, And afflict Athur, and subdue beyond the Phrat; But they also shall perish forever.
24.25: And Bileam arose, and went and returned to his place; and Balak also went upon his way.

25.1: But Israel abode in Shittin; and the people began to commit whoredom with the daughters of Moab;
25.2: And they invited the people to the sacrifices of their idols, and the people did eat and bowed down to their idols.
25.3: And Israel was joined unto Baala Pheor, and the anger of the Lord was kindled against Israel.
25.4: And the Lord said unto Mosheh: Take all the chiefs of the people, and judge, and slay him who is guilty of death before the Lord, over against the sun, that the fierce anger of the Lord may be turned away from Israel.
25.5: And Mosheh said to the judges of Israel: Slay every man his men who have joined themselves to Baala Pheor.
25.6: And, behold, a man of the sons of Israel came and brought to his brethren a Midianitha, in the eyes of Mosheh, and in the eyes of all the congregation of the children of Israel, who were weeping at the door of the tabernacle of ordinance.
25.7: And Phinehas bar Elazar bar Aharon the priest saw, and arose from the midst of the congregation, and took a lance in his hand;
25.8: And he went in after the man, the son of Israel, into the tent, and thrust both of them through, the man, the son of Israel, and the woman, through her belly; and the pestilence was stayed from the children of Israel.
25.9: But they who had died by the pestilence were twenty and four thousand.
25.10: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
25.11: Phinehas the son of Elazar, the son of Aharon, the priest, hath turned away My anger from the children of Israel, in that he was zealous with My zeal among them; and I have not consumed the children of Israel in My jealousy.
25.12: Say therefore to him (that), behold, I decree unto him My covenant of peace;
25.13: And he shall have it and his sons after him; a covenant of priesthood forever, because he hath been zealous before his God, and hath propitiated for the children of Israel.
25.14: And the name of the man of Israel who was slain with the Midianitess was Zimri bar Salu, a chief of the house of his fathers of the house of Shemeon;
25.15: And the name of the woman, the Midianitess, was Kosbe, the daughter of Zur, who was chief of the people of his father’s house in Midian.
25.16: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
25.17: Punish the Midianites and slay them,
25.18: For they afflict you with their snares, with which they ensnare you; as by the occasion of Pheor, and by that of Kosbe, daughter of a prince of Midian, their sister, who was slain on the day of the pestilence in the matter of Pheor.
25.19: And it came to pass after the plague,

26.1: that the Lord spake to Mosheh and to Elazar bar Aharon the priest, saying:
26.2: Take the account of all the congregation of the sons of Israel, from a son of twenty years and upwards by the house of their fathers, everyone that goeth out with the host in Israel.
26.3: And Mosheh and Elazar the priest spake with them, and directed to number them in the plains of Moab, by the Jordan (over against) Jericho, saying:
26.4: From a son of twenty years and upward, as the Lord commanded Mosheh, and the sons of Israel who went forth from the land of Mizraim.
26.5: Reuben, the first-born of Israel: the sons of Reuben, Hanok, the family of Hanok; Phallu, and the family of Phallu;
26.6: of Hezron, the family of Hezron; of Karmi, the family of Karmi.
26.7: These are the families of Reuben, and they who were numbered of them were forty-three thousand seven hundred and thirty.
26.8: And of the sons of Phallu, Eliab;
26.9: And the sons of Eliab, Nemuel, and Dathan, and Abiram: these are Dathan and Abiram who called the congregation that gathered against Mosheh and Aharon in the congregation of Korach, in their gathering against the Lord,
26.10: when the earth opened her mouth and swallowed them with Korach, and the congregation died, being devoured by the fire, two hundred and fifty men; and they became a sign;
26.11: but the sons of Korach died not.
26.12: The sons of Shimeon by their families: of Nemuel, the family of Nemuel; of Jamin, the family of Jamin;
26.13: of Zerach, the family of Zerach; of Shaul, the family of Shaul.
26.14: These are the families of Shemeon, twenty-two thousand two hundred.
26.15: The sons of Gad after their families; of Zephon, the family of Zephon; of Haggi, the family of Haggi; of Shumi, the family of Shumi; of Aggi, the family of Aggi;
26.16: Of Ozni, the family of Ozni; of Heri, the family of Heri;
26.17: of Arod, the family of the Arodi of Areli, the family of Areli.
26.18: These are the families of the Beni Gad, the number of whom was forty thousand five hundred.
26.19: Of the sons of Jehudah, Her and Onan: but Her and Onan died in the land of Kenaan;
26.20: Of the sons of Jehudah after their families: of Shelah, the family of Shelah; of Pherez, the family of Pherez; of Zerach, the family of Zerach.
26.21: Of the sons of Pherez: of Hezron, the family of Hezron; of Hamul, the family of Hamul.
26.22: These are the families of Jehudah; the number of them seventy-six thousand five hundred.
26.23: The sons of Issakar by their families: Tola, the family of Tola; of Phua, the family of the Phuni;
26.24: Of Jasub, the family of Jasub; of Shimron, the family of Shimron.
26.25: These are the families of Issakar; their number sixty-four thousand three hundred.
26.26: The sons of Zebulon by their families: of Sared, the family of Sared; of Elon, the family of Elon; of Jahleel, the family of Jahleel.
26.27: These are the families of Zebulon, by their number sixty thousand five hundred.
26.28: The sons of Joseph by their families, Menasheh and Ephraim,
26.29: The sons of Menasheh: of Makir, the family of Makir; and Makir begat Gilead; of Gilead, the family of Gilead.
26.30: These are the children of Gilead: of Jezar, the family of Jezar; of Helek, the family of Helek;
26.31: And of Asriel, the family of Asrieli; and of Shekem, the family of Shekem;
26.32: And of Shemida, the family of Shemida; and of Hepher, the family of Hepher.
26.33: And Zelophechad bar Hepher had no sons, but daughters; and the names of the daughters of Zelophechad were Mahali, and Nohah, Hegelah, Milchah, and Thirzah.
26.34: These are the families of Menasheh, and their number fifty-two thousand seven hundred.
26.35: These are the sons of Ephraim by their families: of Shuthelah, the family of Shuthelah; of Bekir, the family of Bekir; of Tachan, the family of Tachan.
26.36: And these are the sons of Shuthelah: of Heran, the family of Heran.
26.37: These are the families of the Beni-Ephraim, the number of whom was thirty-two thousand five hundred. These are the sons of Joseph by their families.
26.38: The sons of Benjamin by their families: of Bela, the family of Bela; of Ashbal, the family of Ashbal; of Ahiram, the family of Ahiram;
26.39: Of Shefuphim, the family of Shefuphim; of Hupham, the family of Hupham.
26.40: And the sons of Bela, Arede and Naaman; the family of the Aredi; and of Naaman, the family of Naaman.
26.41: These are the sons of Benjamin after their families, and their number forty-five thousand six hundred.
26.42: These are the children of Dan, after their families: of Shuham, the families of Shuham. These are the families of Dan after their families,
26.43: And the number of the families of Shuham sixty-four thousand four hundred.
26.44: The sons of Asher, after their families: of Jimna, the families of Jimna; of Jeshvi, the families of Jeshvi; of Beriah, the family of Beriah.
26.45: Of the sons of Beriah: of Heber, the family of Heber; of Malkiel, the family of Malkiel.
26.46: But the name of the daughter of Asher was Sarach.
26.47: These are the families of the Beni Asher, by their number fifty-three thousand four hundred.
26.48: The sons of Naphtali, after their families: of Jahziel, the families of Jahziel; of Gunni, the families of Gunni;
26.49: of Jezer, the family of Jezer; of Shelem, the family of Shelem.
26.50: These are the families of Naphtali by their families, and their number forty-five thousand four hundred.
26.51: These were the numbered of the sons of Israel, six hundred and one thousand seven hundred and thirty.
26.52: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
26.53: Unto these thou shalt divide the land for a possession, according to the number of their names.
26.54: To the many thou shalt make large their possession, and to the few thou shalt make their possession small; to each according to his number shalt thou give his inheritance.
26.55: Nevertheless the land shall be divided by lot, according to the names of the tribes of their fathers they shall inherit.
26.56: By the lot shall their inheritance be divided among the many and the few.
26.57: And these are the sons of Levi, after their families: of Gershon, the families of Gershon; of Kehath, the family of Kehath; of Merari, the families of Merari.
26.58: These are the families of Levi: the family of Libni, the family of Hebron, the family of Machli, the family off Mushi, the family of Korach And Kehath begat Amram.
26.59: And the name of Amram’s wife was Jokebed, a daughter of Levi, who was born to Levi, in Mizraim; and she bare unto Amram Aharon, and Mosheh, and Miriam their sister.
26.60: And unto Aharon were born Nadab and Abihu, Elazar and Ithamar.
26.61: But Nadab and Abihu died in their offering strange fire before the Lord.
26.62: And the numbered of them were twenty-three thousand of all the males from a month old and upwards: for they were not numbered among the children of Israel, because no possession was given to them among the children of Israel.
26.63: These (are they whom) Mosheh and Elazar the priest numbered of the sons of Israel, in the plains of Moab, by Jordan, (over against) Jericho.
26.64: But among these there was not a man of them whom Mosheh and Aharon the priest numbered when they counted the children of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai.
26.65: For the Lord had said to them that dying they should die in the wilderness; and not a man of them remained, except Kaleb bar Jephuneh and Jehoshua bar Nun.

27.1: And the daughters of Zelophechad bar Hepher, bar Gilead, bar Makir, bar Menasheh, of the families of Menasheh, bar Joseph, and these are the names of his daughters, Mahelah, Nohah, and Hegelah, and Milchah, and Thirzah,
27.2: Came and stood before Mosheh and Elazar the priest, and before the princes, and all the congregation, at the door of the tabernacle of ordinance, saying:
27.3: Our father died in the wilderness; but he was not among the company which gathered against the Lord in the congregation of Korach, but died through his (own) sin; and he had no sons.
27.4: Why should the name of our father be taken away from among his kindred, because he had no son? Give us an inheritance among the brethren of our father.
27.5: And Mosheh brought their cause before the Lord.
27.6: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
27.7: The daughters of Zelophechad have spoken properly. Give thou to them the possession of an inheritance among the brethren of their father, and transfer to them their father’s inheritance.
27.8: And speak with the children of Israel, saying: If a man die, having no son, you shall make over his inheritance to his daughter;
27.9: And if he have no daughter, you shall give his inheritance to his brethren;
27.10: But if he have no brothers, you shall give his inheritance to the brethren of his father;
27.11: And if his father have no brothers, then shall you give his inheritance to his relative who is next (of kin) to him of his family, and he shall inherit it. And this shall be to the children of Israel for a decree of judgment, as the Lord hath commanded Mosheh.
27.12: And the Lord said unto Mosheh, Go up to this mountain of the Abaraee, and see the land which I have given to the children of Israel;
27.13: And thou shalt see it, and be gathered to thy people, thou also, as Aharon thy brother was gathered.
27.14: As ye rebelled against My Word in the desert of Zin, in the strife of the congregation, to sanctify Me at the waters before their eyes; these are the waters of strife, at Rekem, in the desert of Zin.
27.15: And Mosheh spake before the Lord, saying;
27.16: Let the Lord, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man over the congregation
27.17: who may go out and go in before them, and may lead them out and bring them in; that this congregation may not be as a flock which hath no shepherd.
27.18: And the Lord said to Mosheh, Take to thee Jehoshua bar Nun, a man in whom is the spirit of prophecy, and lay thy hand upon him.
27.19: And make him stand before Elazar the priest, and before all the congregation, and give him charge in their sight.
27.20: And thou shalt confer some of thy honour upon him, that all the congregation of the children of Israel may obey him.
27.21: And he shall stand before Elazar the priest, that he may ask (counsel) for him by the judgment of Uraia before the Lord: upon his word shall they go out, and upon his word shall they come in, he and all the sons of Israel with him, even all the congregation.
27.22: And Mosheh did as the Lord commanded him, and took Jehoshua, and made him to stand before Elazar the priest, and all the congregation;
27.23: And he laid his hands upon him, and gave him charge, as the Lord spake by Mosheh.

28.1: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
28.2: instruct the children of Israel, and say to them: My oblation, the ordained bread for My oblations to be received with acceptance, shall you observe to offer in its time.
28.3: And thou shalt say to them: This is the oblation which you shall offer before the Lord; two lambs of the year unblemished daily, for a perpetual burnt offering.
28.4: The one lamb shalt thou perform in the morning, and the second lamb between the suns.
28.5: And with one-tenth of three seahs of flour for the mincha sprinkled with the fourth of a hin of beaten oil.
28.6: It is a perpetual burnt offering, which was made in the mountain of Sinai, to be received with acceptance (as) an oblation before the Lord.
28.7: And its libation shall be the fourth of a hin for each lamb; in the sanctuary shall the libation of old wine be poured out before the Lord.
28.8: And the second lamb shalt thou perform between the suns, as the morning offering; and thou shalt make its libation (in like manner) an oblation to be received with acceptance before the Lord.
28.9: But on the Sabbath day two lambs of the year unblemished, and two-tenths of flour for the mincha sprinkled with oil, and its libation.
28.10: It is the Sabbath burnt offering which shall be performed on the Sabbath, together with the perpetual burnt offering and its libation.
28.11: And in the beginnings of your months you shall offer a burnt offering before the Lord; two young bullocks, and one ram, lambs of the year, seven, unblemished.
28.12: And three tenths of flour sprinkled with oil for each bullock, and two-tenths of flour for a mincha sprinkled with oil for the one ram,
28.13: And a tenth of flour for a mincha sprinkled with oil for each lamb: it is a burnt offering to be received with acceptance as an oblation before the Lord.
28.14: And their libations a half hina of wine shall be for the bullock, and the third of a hina for the ram, and a quarter of a hina for a lamb: this is the burnt offering for the beginning of the month, at its renewal; so shall it be for all the beginnings of the months of the year.
28.15: And one kid of the goats for a sin offering before the Lord, beside the perpetual burnt offering, shalt thou make with its libation.
28.16: And in the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is the Pascha before the Lord.
28.17: And on the fifteenth day of this month is the feast: seven days you shall eat unleavened (bread).
28.18: On the first day shall be a holy convocation; you shall not do any servile work;
28.19: But offer the oblation of a burnt offering before the Lord; two young bullocks and one ram, and seven lambs of the year without blemish shall you have;
28.20: And their mincha of flour mingled with oil, three tenths for the bullock and two-tenths for the ram you shall make;
28.21: a tenth shall you make for one lamb, so for the seven lambs.
28.22: And one goat for a sin offering to make atonement for you;
28.23: Besides the burnt sacrifice of the morning which is the perpetual burnt sacrifice, you shall make these.
28.24: After the manner of these you shall do by the day for seven days; it is the bread of the oblation to be received with acceptance before the Lord; (with) the perpetual burnt offering and its libation shall it be made.
28.25: And on the seventh day there shall be a holy convocation, (when) you may do no servile work.
28.26: But on the day of the Firstfruits, when you bring the new thank-offering before the Lord in your expletion, there shall be a holy convocation; no servile work shall you do,
28.27: But offer a burnt offering to be received with favour before the Lord; two young bullocks, one ram, seven lambs of the year;
28.28: And their mincha of flour mingled with oil, three tenths for one bullock,
28.29: two-tenths for the ram, a tenth for each lamb of the seven lambs;
28.30: One kid of the goats to make an atonement for you;
28.31: Beside the perpetual burnt sacrifice and its mincha you shall (make) them unblemished, and their libations.

29.1: And in the seventh month, on the first of the month, you shall have a holy convocation, and do no servile work; it shall be a day of the sounding of the trumpet to you.
29.2: And you shall make a burnt sacrifice to be received with favour before the Lord: one young bullock, one ram, lambs of the year seven, unblemished,
29.3: and their mincha of flour mingled with oil, three tenths for the bullock, two-tenths for the ram,
29.4: And one-tenth for each of the seven lambs;
29.5: And one kid of the goats for a sin offering to make an atonement for you;
29.6: Beside the offering of the month, and its mincha, and the perpetual sacrifice and its mincha, and their libations, as proper for them, to be received with favour, an oblation before the Lord.
29.7: And on the tenth of this seventh month you shall have a holy convocation, and afflict your souls; you shall do no labour,
29.8: but offer a burnt offering before the Lord to be received with favour: one young bullock, one ram, lambs of the year seven, unblemished shall you have;
29.9: And their mincha of flour mingled with oil; three tenths for the bullock, two-tenths for the ram,
29.10: And a single tenth for each of the seven lambs;
29.11: One kid of the goats for a sin offering, beside the sin offering of the expiations, and the perpetual sacrifice, its mincha and their libations.
29.12: And on the fifteenth day of the seventh month you shall have a holy convocation; no servile labour shall you do, but celebrate a festival before the Lord seven days;
29.13: And offer a burnt sacrifice, an oblation to be received with favour before the Lord; thirteen young bullocks, two rams, lambs of the year fourteen, unblemished shall they be;
29.14: And their mincha of flour mingled with oil, three tenths to one bullock for the thirteen bullocks, two-tenths for each ram,
29.15: And one-tenth for each of the fourteen lambs,
29.16: And one kid of the goats for a sin offering, beside the perpetual sacrifice, its mincha and libation.
29.17: And on the second day you shall offer twelve young bullocks, two rams, fourteen unblemished lambs of the year,
29.18: and the minchas and libations for the bullocks, for the rams and the lambs, as is proper for their number;
29.19: And one kid of the goats, a sin offering, beside the perpetual sacrifice, its mincha and libation.
29.20: And on the third day eleven bullocks, two rams, fourteen unblemished lambs of the year;
29.21: And their minchas and libations for the bullocks, the rams, and the lambs, as befitteth their number;
29.22: And one kid for a sin offering, beside the perpetual sacrifice, its mincha and libation.
29.23: On the fourth day ten bullocks, two rams, lambs of the year unblemished fourteen;
29.24: Their minchas and libations for the bullocks, rams, and lambs by their number, as it is proper;
29.25: And one kid of the goats for a sin offering, beside the perpetual sacrifice, its mincha and libation.
29.26: And on the fifth day nine bullocks, two rams, lambs of the year unblemished fourteen;
29.27: The minchas and libations for the bullocks, rams, and lambs after their number, as it is proper;
29.28: And one kid for a sin offering, beside the perpetual sacrifice and its libation.
29.29: And on the sixth day eight bullocks, two rams, lambs of the year unblemished fourteen;
29.30: The minchas and libations for the bullocks, rams, and lambs by their number, as is proper;
29.31: And one kid for the sin offering, beside the perpetual sacrifice, its mincha and libation.
29.32: And on the seventh day seven bullocks, two rams, fourteen lambs of the year unblemished;
29.33: The minchas and libations for the bullocks, rams, and lambs by their number, as is proper;
29.34: And one kid for the sin offering, beside the perpetual sacrifice, its mincha and libation.
29.35: On the eighth day you shall have all assembly; no servile work shall you do,
29.36: But offer a sacrifice, all oblation to be received with favour before the Lord; one bullock, one ram, seven Iambs of the year unblemished;
29.37: The minchas and libations for the bullock, the ram, and the lambs, as proper, according to their number;
29.38: And one kid for a sill offering, beside the perpetual sacrifice, its mincha and libation.
29.39: These shall you offer before the Lord in your solemnities, beside your vows and your free-will offerings with your burnt sacrifices, their minchas and their libations, and with your sanctified victims.

30.1: And Mosheh spake to the sons of Israel according to all that the Lord commanded Mosheh.
30.2: And Mosheh spake with the heads of the tribes of the Beni Israel, saying: This is the word which the Lord hath commanded:
30.3: When a man shall make a vow before the Lord, or swear an oath to bind a bond upon his soul, he shall not make void his word; according to all that hath come out of his mouth he shall perform.
30.4: And if a woman make a vow before the Lord, and bind (herself) with a bond in her father’s house, (being) in her youth,
30.5: And her father shall hear her vow, and the obligation she hath bound upon her soul, and her father be silent to her, then all her vows shall stand, and every bond that she hath bound upon her soul shall be confirmed.
30.6: But if her father prohibit (or undo) them on the day that he heareth, all the vows and the bonds that she hath bound upon her soul shall not stand, and she shall be forgiven before the Lord, because her father undid them.
30.7: And if she hath a husband, and taketh a vow upon her, or if her lips pronounce that which becometh binding upon her soul,
30.8: and her husband heard and was silent to her on the day that he heard, her vows shall stand, and the obligation she hath bound upon her soul be confirmed:
30.9: But if her husband on the day that he heareth shall prohibit them, the vows which are on her and the utterance of her lips which became binding on her soul shall be void, and be forgiven her before the Lord.
30.10: But every vow of the widow, or of one divorced, which she hath bound upon her soul, shall be confirmed upon her.
30.11: And if (while in her husband’s house) she had vowed, or had bound aught upon her soul with an oath,
30.12: And her husband heard and was silent to her, and did not prohibit them, all her vows shall be confirmed, every bond with which she hath bound her soul shall be confirmed.
30.13: But if indeed her husband shall make them void in the day that he heard, that which her lips expressed in her vow and in the binding of her soul shall not be confirmed; her husband hath made them void, and she shall be absolved before the Lord.
30.14: Every vow and every covenant (oath) to chastise the soul, her husband may confirm it, or her husband may make it void.
30.15: But if her husband was entirely silent to her from day to day, then he hath confirmed all her vows, or whatever bonds (she taketh) upon her, he confirmeth them, because he was silent to her on the day that he heard.
30.16: But if he shall indeed make them void after (the day that) he had heard, then he shall bear her sin.
30.17: These are the statutes which the Lord commanded Mosheh between a man and his wife, (and) between a father and his daughter, in her youth in her father’s house.

31.1: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
31.2: Avenge the children of Israel of the Midianites; afterward thou shalt be gathered to thy people.
31.3: And Mosheh spake with the people, saying: Arm, of you, men for the host against Midian, to avenge this people of the Lord upon Midian:
31.4: A thousand of a tribe, a thousand of a tribe, of all the tribes or Israel, shall you send to the host.
31.5: And from the thousands of Israel there were chosen a thousand of a tribe, twelve thousand armed for the host.
31.6: And Mosheh sent them one thousand of a tribe to array them, and Phinehas bar Elazar the priest, with the host, and the holy vessels, and the Jubela trumpets in his hand.
31.7: And the host gathered against Midian, as tile Lord had commanded Mosheh; and they slaughtered every male.
31.8: But the kings of Midian they killed with their slain, Evi, and Rekem, and Zur, and Chur, and Reba, five kings of Midian, and Bileam bar Beor, they killed with the sword.
31.9: And the sons of Israel took the women of Midian captives, with their children and all their cattle, and all their flocks and all their goods they despoiled.
31.10: And all their cities where they dwelt, and their houses of worship, they burned with fire.
31.11: And they took all the spoil, and all the prey of man and of cattle,
31.12: and brought the captives, and the prey, and the spoil, to Mosheh, and to Elazar the priest, and to all the congregation of the Beni Israel, to the camp in the fields of Moab, by the Jordan, over against Jericho.
31.13: And Mosheh and Elazar the priest and all the princes of the congregation went out to meet them, without the camp.
31.14: But Mosheh was angry with those who had been appointed over the host, the captains of thousands and the captains of hundreds, who came from the battle.
31.15: And Mosheh said to them, Have you spared every woman?
31.16: Behold, these it was (who caused) the sons of Israel, through the counsel of Bileam, to do wickedly before the Lord in the matter of Peor, and the plague came upon the congregation of the Lord.
31.17: But now, slay every male among the children, and every woman who hath known a man you shall slay.
31.18: But all the females who have not known a man ye may preserve alive unto you.
31.19: And you, abide without the camp seven days; whoever have destroyed life or touched the dead, sprinkle yourselves on the third day, and on the seventh day yourselves and your captives.
31.20: And every garment, and whatever is made of skin, and every work of goat’s hair, and every vessel of wood you shall sprinkle.
31.21: And Elazar the priest said to the men of war who came from the battle, This is the decree of the law which the Lord hath commanded Mosheh:
31.22: Only the gold, and the silver, the brass, iron, tin, and lead,
31.23: everything that can abide in the fire, you shall make to go through fire, and it shall be clean; nevertheless it shall be sprinkled with the water of sprinkling; and whatever may not abide the fire you shall make to pass through water.
31.24: And cleanse your garments on the seventh day; purify yourselves, and afterwards come into the camp.
31.25: And the Lord spake with Mosheh, saying:
31.26: Take the account of the spoil of the captives, man and beast; thou, Elazar the priest, and the chief fathers of the congregation,
31.27: And divide the spoil among the men who fought the battle, who went forth in the host, and among all the congregation:
31.28: And separate a portion before the Lord from (that of) the men who fought the battle, who went forth in the host, one living thing in five hundred, of man and beast, oxen, asses, and sheep.
31.29: Take it of their half, and give it to Elazar the priest, for a separation before the Lord.
31.30: And of the half (belonging) to the children of Israel, take one of every fifty, of man, of oxen, sheep, and all cattle, and give them to the Levites who keep charge of the tabernacle of the Lord.
31.31: And Mosheh and Elazar the priest did as the Lord commanded Mosheh.
31.32: And the booty, the rest of the prey which the people who went forth to the war had taken, was, sheep six hundred and seventy-five thousand,
31.35: persons, women who had not known man, every soul thirty-two thousand.
31.36: And the half portion of the men who had gone out to the war, the number was, sheep three hundred and thirty-seven thousand five hundred;
31.37: And that which was brought up before the Lord, of the sheep six hundred and seventy-five;
31.38: And of the thirty-six thousand oxen, the portion brought before the Lord seventy-two.
31.39: And the asses, thirty thousand five hundred, of which the portion brought before the Lord sixty-one.
31.40: And the persons sixteen thousand, those of them brought before the Lord thirty-two persons.
31.41: And Mosheh gave the separation brought up before the Lord to Elazar the priest, as the Lord had commanded Mosheh.
31.42: And of the children of Israel’s half, which Mosheh divided from (that) of the men who had gone out in the host,
31.43: And the half part for the congregation as, sheep three hundred and thirty-seven thousand five hundred,
31.45: and asses thirty thousand five hundred,
31.47: And Mosheh took from the children of Israel’s half one portion of fifty of man and beast, and gave them to the Levites who kept charge of the Lord’s tabernacle, as the Lord had commanded Mosheh.
31.48: And they who had been appointed over the thousands of the host, the captains of thousands, and the captains of hundreds, came to Mosheh,
31.49: And said to Mosheh, Thy servants have taken the account of the men who went forth to the war with us, and there is not wanting one man of us.
31.50: And we bring an oblation before the Lord of what each man hath found, vessels of gold, chains, bracelets, rings, amulets, and brooches, to make atonement for our souls before the Lord.
31.51: And Mosheh and Elazar the priest took the gold of them, every fabricated vessel.
31.52: And all the gold of the separation which the captains of thousands and of hundreds separated before the Lord was: sixteen thousand seven hundred and fifty shekels;
31.53: for the men of the host had taken spoil, every man for himself.
31.54: And Mosheh and Elazar the priest took the gold from the captains of thousands and of hundreds, and brought it into the tabernacle of ordinance, a memorial of the sons of Israel before the Lord.

32.1: Now the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad possessed much cattle, exceedingly many; and they saw the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead, and, behold, the region was a place fit for folds of cattle.
32.2: And the sons of Gad and the sons of Reuben came and spake to Mosheh and to Elazar the priest, and to the heads of the congregation, saying:
32.3: Maklelta and Malbasta and the Priests of Beth-Nemrin, and Beth-Hesh-bena, and Baale Debaba, and Seath, (the sepulchre of Mosheh,) and Beon,
32.4: The land which the Lord smote before the congregation of Israel, is a country fitted for cattle folds, and thy servants have cattle.
32.5: And they said, If we have found grace in thine eyes, let this land be given to thy servants for a possession, and let us not go over the Jordan.
32.6: But Mosheh said to the sons of Gad and to the sons of Reuben, Shall your brethren go in to fight, and you sit down here?
32.7: And why turn you away the heart of the sons of Israel from going over to the land which the Lord hath given to them?
32.8: Thus did your fathers when I sent them from Rekem Giah to survey the land.
32.9: They went up to the stream of Ethkela, and saw the land, and subverted the heart of the sons of Israel, that they might not go in unto the land that the Lord had given to them;
32.10: And the Lord’s anger was kindled that day, and He sware, saying:
32.11: If the men who have come out of Mizraim, from twenty years old and upward, shall see the land which I covenanted to Abraham, to Izhak, and to Jakob; for they have not been wholly after my fear.
32.12: Only Kaleb bar Jephuneh, the Kenezite, and Jehoshua bar Nun, for they have been wholly after the fear of the Lord.
32.13: And the Lord’s anger was strong against Israel, and he made them linger in the wilderness forty years, until all the generation that did wickedly before the Lord had been consumed.
32.14: And, behold, you have risen up after your fathers, the disciples of the men of sin, to add yet to the fierce displeasure of the Lord against Israel.
32.15: For if you turn again from (following) after His service, He will yet make you remain in the wilderness, and you will destroy all this people.
32.16: And they came near to him, and said: We will build here sheepfolds for our cattle and cities for our families;
32.17: And we will go forth eagerly, armed, before the sons of Israel, to bring them into their place; and our families shall abide in cities defenced against the inhabitants of the land:
32.18: Nor will we return to our homes till the sons of Israel shall possess every man his inheritance.
32.19: For we will not inherit with them over the Jordan and beyond; for we receive our possession on the eastward side of the Jordan.
32.20: And Mosheh said to them: If you will do this; if you will go armed before the people of the Lord to war,
32.21: and (a host) of you all armed will pass the Jordan before the people of the Lord, until He shall have driven out the enemy before Him,
32.22: And the land have been subdued before the Lord’s people, then afterward you shall return, and be guiltless before the Lord and with Israel, and this land shall be to you for an inheritance before the Lord.
32.23: But if you do it not, behold, you have sinned before the Lord; and know, that your sin will find you.
32.24: Build you cities for your families, and folds for your sheep, and do that which hath come from your mouth.
32.25: And the tribe of the Beni Gad and of the Beni Reuben spake to Mosheh, saying: Thy servants will do as my lord commandeth.
32.26: Our little ones, our wives, our flocks, and all our cattle shall be here in the cities of Gilead;
32.27: But thy servants, a host all armed, will pass over before the people of the Lord to war, as our lord speaketh.
32.28: And Mosheh commanded concerning them Elazar the priest, and Jehoshua bar Nun, and the chief fathers of the tribes of the Beni Israel.
32.29: And Mosheh said to them, If the sons of Gad and of Reuben pass over the Jordan with you, all armed for war, before the Lord’s people, and the land be subdued before you, then shall you give them the land of Gilead for a possession.
32.30: But if they go not over armed with you, they shall inherit among you in the land of Kenaan.
32.31: But the sons of Gad and of Reuben answered, saying: As the Lord hath spoken to thy servants, so will we do.
32.32: We will pass over armed before the people of the Lord into the land of Kenaan, that the possession of our inheritance may be on the other side Jordan.
32.33: And Mosheh gave to them, to the sons of Gad, and to the sons of Reuben, and to the half tribe of Menasheh bar Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amoraah, and the kingdom of Og the king of Mathanan, the land with the cities thereof in the coasts, (even) the cities of the country round about.
32.34: And the sons of Gad built Dibon, and Ataroth, and Aroer,
32.35: and Ataroth Shophan, and Jazer, and Jagbeha,
32.36: and Beth-nimra, and Beth-haran, fenced cities and sheepfolds.
32.37: And the sons of Reuben built Heshbon, and Elhala, and Kirjathaim,
32.38: And Nebo, and Baal Meon, changing their names, and Sibama; and they called by their names the names of the cities which they built.
32.39: And the sons of Makir bar Menasheh went unto Gilead, and subdued it, and cast out the Amoraah who were in it.
32.40: And Mosheh gave Gilead to Makir bar Menasheh, and he dwelt therein.
